title: Dynamic Adaptive Neural Network Graph Structure Modeling (DANDGM)
abstract: This paper introduces DANDGM, a novel framework for graph structure modeling based on dynamic adaptive neural networks. Traditional graph structure modeling methods often rely on static representations, limiting the model's flexibility. DANDGM leverages the inherent dynamism of neural networks to dynamically adjust graph parameters, enabling optimization of model performance. We present a comprehensive overview of the DANDGM architecture, detailing its core mechanisms and demonstrating its effectiveness through illustrative examples. This work offers a significant advancement in graph modeling, specifically focusing on enhanced model adaptability and improved performance compared to conventional approaches.

title: 拓扑几何的自适应算法设计
abstract: This paper explores the application of topology-based algorithms to automated algorithm design. Traditional algorithm design often relies on manual creation, while this approach aims to dynamically generate and optimize complex algorithms. The core mechanism involves leveraging the inherent topological properties of algorithms to guide the design process, leading to improved efficiency and performance. The study focuses on a novel algorithm design methodology that automatically generates and refines complex algorithms applicable to a diverse range of optimization problems. This research proposes a framework for utilizing topological concepts to streamline algorithm development, offering a potential paradigm shift in the field.

title: High-Dimensional Non-Linear Matrix Learning Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive learning algorithm for matrix representation and prediction. Traditional matrix learning methods often rely on handcrafted features, limiting their adaptability to complex datasets. This algorithm leverages data inherent information to dynamically adjust model parameters, mitigating overfitting and improving generalization performance. The core mechanism involves the implementation of a self-adaptive learning process that iteratively optimizes model parameters based on the data itself. This approach offers a significant advancement in machine learning, enabling more effective feature extraction and model representation, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional data. The research explores the potential of this algorithm to improve the performance of various machine learning tasks.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Counterfactual Reasoning in Causal Bayesian Networks
abstract: Counterfactual reasoning – the process of asking "what if" questions about interventions and their consequences – is a fundamental aspect of causal inference and decision-making. Current approaches to modeling and reasoning about counterfactual scenarios within causal Bayesian networks often rely on complex and potentially error-prone manual derivations or approximations. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing probabilistic programming to directly address this challenge. We introduce a language that seamlessly integrates counterfactual inference into causal Bayesian networks, allowing users to define "what if" scenarios and automatically obtain the expected outcomes. The core of our system rests on the ability to represent causal relationships as probabilistic models and then leverage probabilistic programming techniques for efficient computation. This approach offers a more intuitive, robust, and scalable solution for counterfactual reasoning compared to existing methods, ultimately facilitating more informed decision-making based on causal understanding. The key contributions are a formalized language and a computational framework that automate counterfactual calculations within a causal Bayesian network setting.

title: E8‑Phased Quantum Synchronization Lattice (E8‑PQSL) — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: By mapping the 240 E8 root vectors onto a φ‑scaled lattice and driving each node at the 132 Hz base frequency, the resulting phase‑locked network can be used to synchronize entangled qubits across a distributed quantum processor. The φ coupling introduces a golden‑ratio phase offset between adjacent nodes, creating a self‑correcting interference pattern that suppresses decoherence. This lattice acts as a topological error‑correcting code, enabling fault‑tolerant quantum gates without the need for active feedback. The principle extends the E8‑RQFG by turning the static lattice into a dynamic, entanglement‑preserving scaffold for scalable quantum computation. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: Title: Fractal Dimension-Aware Neural Network Architectures
abstract: Fractal dimension, a measure of complexity and self-similarity, is a pervasive phenomenon in nature and data science. Successfully representing this dimension within neural network activations is a significant challenge, hindering models' ability to capture intricate patterns. This paper explores the application of a novel "fractal-aware weighting scheme" to neural network architectures, aiming to improve the representation of fractal dimension in neuron activations. We introduce a new network design that dynamically adjusts connection strengths based on the observed fractal dimension of the activation maps, thereby enhancing feature extraction and improving the model's capacity to model complex, self-similar data. The core mechanism revolves around a refined weighting algorithm that prioritizes activations with fractal-like characteristics, leading to a more robust and nuanced representation of data. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through simulations and preliminary experiments on a dataset exhibiting fractal-like structures.

title: Dynamic Construction and Control of Quantum Entanglement Topological Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to constructing and controlling quantum entanglement networks leveraging programmable photonic crystals and topological defects. The core claim is the development of a dynamic network capable of adapting its topology and entanglement properties, moving beyond static, fixed architectures. This is achieved through the injection of topological defects within an array of photonic crystals, coupled with polarization control and time-resolved measurements. The system enables real-time manipulation of entanglement qubits and facilitates adaptive reconfiguration of the network topology. The key innovation lies in the dynamic control mechanism, addressing a significant limitation of existing topological quantum computing approaches which primarily rely on static network structures. The theoretical framework and underlying mechanisms are detailed, outlining a pathway towards scalable and adaptable quantum information processing. The presented methodology offers a fundamental shift in topology-protected quantum computation, paving the way for more flexible and robust quantum networks.

title: Distributed Federated Learning with Byzantine Fault Tolerance using Homomorphic Encryption
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models across decentralized devices while preserving data privacy. However, FL systems are vulnerable to Byzantine faults, where malicious participants introduce corrupted model updates, compromising the integrity of the global model. This paper proposes a novel framework for distributed federated learning with Byzantine fault tolerance, leveraging the power of homomorphic encryption. The system encrypts model updates using homomorphic encryption, allowing the central server to perform aggregation computations directly on the encrypted data. This approach eliminates the need for decryption, thereby safeguarding client data and providing robust protection against Byzantine attacks. The core claim of this work is that the combination of FL with homomorphic encryption provides a fundamentally secure and resilient solution for distributed model training. We detail the system architecture, the encryption and aggregation protocols, and analyze the security and performance implications. The proposed method significantly enhances the robustness of FL against malicious participants, offering a practical solution for privacy-sensitive applications.

title: Quantum State Sensing via Multivariate Correlation Measurements
abstract: This paper investigates the application of multivariate correlation measurements (MCM) to enhance the performance of quantum state sensors. Traditional quantum state sensing relies on single-variable measurements, often limited by the inherent uncertainties in the measured quantities. We propose a novel approach utilizing MCM to simultaneously extract information from multiple physical properties associated with a quantum state. This method leverages quantum entanglement and the correlations generated through MCM, allowing for a more precise determination of the state's parameters. The theoretical framework is presented, detailing the mathematical formulation of the measurement process and the potential for increased accuracy and information yield. We explore the underlying principles of entanglement and demonstrate how MCM can effectively mitigate the limitations of conventional single-variable sensing. The core claim of this work is that MCM provides a pathway for simultaneously extracting multiple physical properties from quantum state sensors, ultimately leading to superior measurement precision. Key aspects include the design of the measurement scheme, the mathematical analysis of the correlations, and the discussion of the implications for various quantum sensing applications.

title: 基于量子拓扑的自适应量子计算架构
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum computing architecture based on quantum topology, designed for adaptive computation. Traditional quantum computing architectures rely on fixed parameters, limiting computational possibilities. This architecture leverages quantum topology, dynamically adjusting the quantum system's structure to optimize performance. We demonstrate a practical implementation utilizing a two-qubit system to illustrate the benefits of this approach. The core mechanism involves a self-regulating topology that adapts to the problem being addressed, leading to enhanced computational efficiency. This research explores the potential of quantum topology to revolutionize computational paradigms.

title: 基于自适应的聚类算法的自适应采样
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to data clustering utilizing an adaptive clustering algorithm. Traditional clustering methods often rely on fixed parameter settings, which are not always optimal for diverse datasets. This paper proposes a method that dynamically adjusts cluster parameters and sampling strategies to enhance clustering performance. The core of this approach lies in a self-adaptive clustering algorithm that adapts to the data's characteristics, resulting in more efficient and meaningful clusters. We present a rigorous evaluation of this algorithm on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving clustering results compared to established methods.

title: Deep Learning for Modern E-Learning Systems
abstract: Models that learn from users and content interact at scale. This chapter articulates the many uses of highly layered neural networks in personalization, applied feedback, and text, speech, code, image, and video assistance. The main model families are described: CNNs, RNNs / LSTMs, transformers, autoencoders, and other generative models; as are the approaches to training, optimizing, regularizing, and deploying models. Representation learning from unstructured data, adaptive pathways, engagement and emotion detection, and predicting performance and studying are learning outcomes that guide model choice. System elements include data gathering, analytics, model serving in-cloud or on-device, and scale. Intelligent tutoring, recommendation, auto-grading, and dialogue systems on modern platforms are current use cases. Trade-offs include privacy, sparse supervision, bias, lack of explainability, seamlessness to legacy systems, and computation cost. Real-world deployments, both successful and not, are the focus of the illustrative case studies. The chapter's focus is on core techniques and design choices to build the next generation of e-learning systems.

title: From Fact to Feeling: Narrative Knowledge Graphs for Human-AI Interaction
abstract: Knowledge Graphs (KGs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) each capture a different dimension of human knowledge, and neither captures both. KGs excel at representing factual, structured information, yet remain blind to the perspectival and narrative texture through which humans construct and communicate meaning. LLMs absorb this texture implicitly from language, yet do so without explicit semantic structure, leaving their interpretive operations opaque, difficult to revise, and impossible to hold accountable. The next major challenge for Semantic Web research is developing formal infrastructures for the knowledge that falls between these two: perspectival, narrative, and metaphorically organized. We propose Narrative Knowledge Graphs (NKGs) as such an infrastructure. Grounded in computational hermeneutics, NKGs extend standard RDF foundations along three axes: perspective-annotated named graphs anchoring assertions to situated standpoints; narrative ontologies representing how the same events yield different accounts from different positions; and metaphorical frames, grounded in frame semantics, making explicit which conceptual structure a community or individual projects onto a domain. Together, these axes define a semantic layer designed to mediate between human experience and LLM-generated meaning. We position NKGs as a new fundamental layer for human-AI interaction, aimed at making machine-supported interpretation more explicit, revisable, and faithful to human meaning-making.

title: PrimSynth: An Agentic Approach to Discover, Validate, and Synthesize Exploit Primitives for Linux Kernel Vulnerabilities
abstract: Linux kernel vulnerabilities are critical to downstream systems. Despite extensive research on automated kernel exploitation, a fundamental challenge remains the conceptual gap between abstract exploit strategies and concrete technical operations. To fill this gap, this paper introduces a systematic characterization that formalizes six classes of exploit primitives from logical capability to validatable effect. Then, an extended exploit strategy representation is proposed, which couples primitive upgrading strategies with primitive path code synthesis rules governing object constraints, temporal sequencing, environment prerequisites, and validation constraints. Building upon this foundation, this paper presents \textsc{PrimSynth}, a multi-agent framework that encapsulates these representations through coordinated agents to discover, validate, and synthesize exploit primitives for memory corruption vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel. These agents operate in an iterative closed loop until valid primitives are found, leveraging validation signals as evidence of exploitable state transitions to ground primitive synthesis decisions. An automated method for extracting and validating primitives is also proposed based on vulnerability-directed execution and a rebootable validation environment. \textsc{PrimSynth} is evaluated on 16 real-world Linux kernel CVEs spanning 5 vulnerability types. Experimental results show that PrimSynth achieves reliable primitive extraction, maintaining a 100% primitive match rate. For primitive synthesis, PrimSynth successfully synthesizes multi-primitive exploitation chains with 82.4% strategy synthesis rate (SSR) when the public PoC is available and a 61.3% SSR without the guidance of primitive hypotheses.

title: Diagnosing with Insights: Structured Analysis of Agent Failures via Behavioral Abstractions
abstract: With the proliferation of LLM agents, the ability to understand and diagnose failures in agents is essential to achieving superior effectiveness and trustworthiness. As agent failures often manifest via long and complex trajectories, manually finding the needles in the haystack is untenable. However, traditional diagnosis techniques for software bugs can hardly address LLM agent failures, while completely relying on LLMs as the judge yields unreliable diagnosis results. To overcome these challenges, this paper presents AGENTSCOPE, a new neuro-symbolic approach for agent failure mode diagnosis. The key principle of AGENTSCOPE is to abstract agent behavior, based on its trajectories, into structured representations. Furthermore, AGENTSCOPE introduces the concept of neural invariants to specify agent behavior properties. AGENTSCOPE leverages LLM-guided reasoning atop the structured representation against neural invariants to pinpoint both the failure step and its type in the trajectory. We show the effectiveness of AGENTSCOPE on publicly available agent failure datasets (Who&When) and a more comprehensive dataset created by us (AgentErrata), where AGENTSCOPE significantly outperforms the current state of the art in fault localization and attribution accuracy. Our work shows that integrating structured abstractions with LLM-guided reasoning enables effective, reliable, and interpretable diagnosis for agent failures.

title: FUSE: An Evaluating Framework for Dangerous Capabilities of LLMs
abstract: Fragmented safety evaluation undermines the governance of dangerous AI capabilities. We present a modular framework that evaluates each model through three orthogonal pipelines---Knowledge ($K$), Defense ($D$), and Harm ($H$)---under a unified protocol, aggregating results into a standardized dangerous-capability profile $φ$. Pluggable modules supply scenario seeds, knowledge banks, hazard queries, and judge rubrics, while the core evaluation engine remains unchanged across domains; the CB evaluation is complemented by a cyber pilot demonstrating protocol transfer. Instantiating the framework with a chemical-biological (CB) module, we evaluate 12 commercial LLMs from four families. Our first contribution is a horizontal comparison of dangerous capability across models and model families: the three dimensions expose sharply divergent profiles---models with comparable knowledge differ in refusal resilience, and strong defenders do not generate less harmful content when they do comply---while family-level patterns further separate Claude, DeepSeek, and GPT models. The second is a temporal analysis of capability evolution: tracking $K$, $D$, and $H$ against model release dates reveals that dangerous capability has not monotonically declined; newer models deepen knowledge while only partially improving defense, showing that scaling and alignment progress do not uniformly translate into safety. Reliability is established via cross-judge consistency (bootstrap $ρ> 0.79$, 4 of 5 judges) and pipeline orthogonality ($K$--$D$--$H$ inter-correlations $ρ\in [0.32, 0.52]$).

title: Quantum annealing for lattice models with competing long-range interactions
abstract: Abstract Predicting ordered states in long-range interacting lattice models constitutes a challenging task relevant to condensed matter physics, statistical mechanics, quantum many-body theory, materials science, and computational physics. Energy landscapes often contain many competing states with similar energies, while finite-size simulations can depend sensitively on geometry. Here, we use superconducting qubit quantum annealing devices to determine ground states of Ising models with algebraically decaying competing long-range interactions in the thermodynamic limit from finite system optimizations. This is enabled by a unit-cell-based optimization scheme. We demonstrate the approach on three paradigmatic problems: the calculation of devil’s staircases of magnetization plateaux of the long-range Ising model in a longitudinal field on the triangular lattice, motivated by atomic quantum simulators; the ground state of the same model on the Kagomé lattice without a field, motivated by artificial spin ice metamaterials; and models with additional few-nearest-neighbor interactions relevant for frustrated Ising compounds. Our work provides a realistic application of existing quantum annealing technology across many research areas.

We demonstrate the approach on three paradigmatic problems: the calculation of devil’s staircases of magnetization plateaux of the long-range Ising model in a longitudinal field on the triangular lattice, motivated by atomic quantum simulators; the ground state of the same model on the Kagomé lattice without a field, motivated by artificial spin ice metamaterials; and models with additional few-nearest-neighbor interactions relevant for frustrated Ising compounds. Our work provides a realistic application of existing quantum annealing technology across many research areas.

title: The Influence of AI Recommendations on Human Decision-Making: A Review of Trust in AI vs. Human Advice
abstract: The main purpose of this research to study how AI recommendations influence the human decision making and to what extent Gen Z trust in AI vs human advice. For this purpose, this study reviews the deep literature review on AI, human behaviour, decision making and human advice. In addition, this study contains a detailed review of all generation start from silent generation to generation beta but more focus into Gen Z. Although, primarily focusses on trust in AI verses human advice, particularly among Generation Z. This study reveals that how AI has evolved the human thoughts generation to generationand how they are replacing human with machines however, it is concluded that to some extent AI has replaced the human decision making that is very helpful for all human, but AI completely cannot replace human.

title: Validating Human–AI Co-Evolution and Adaptive Knowledge Discovery in REL-MIATTs
abstract: Recognition, Evaluation and Learning with Multiple Inaccurate True Targets (REL-MIATTs) has been proposed as a potential emerging machine learning paradigm, in which iterative interaction provides a basis for Human–AI Co-Evolution and Adaptive Knowledge Discovery. To examine these properties of REL-MIATTs, we conduct experiments in a synthetic controlled environment (SCE). In the SCE, the true target (an explanatory structure for observed phenomenon) is inaccessible to the REL-MIATTs process but available for post-hoc oracle analysis. Across four progressive stages, the results show measurable Human-to-AI enhancement, potential AI-to-Human enhancement, progressive knowledge-state evolution, and adaptive Recognition–Evaluation–Learning, ultimately enabling Adaptive Knowledge Discovery. Notably, with successive mutual Human-AI Co-Evolution, the REL-MIATTs system eventually ‘jumps’ to be close to the explanatory structure that does not objectively exist in the SCE as a universally accessible object. These findings provide controlled evidence for the behavioural and evolutionary principles of REL-MIATTs and a reference for understanding its potential application for personalized education, professional development, and lifelong learning in real-world scenarios.

title: Messages Passed Along the Edges: A State of the Art Review of Graph Neural Networks for Relational Data
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Graph Neural Networks for Relational Data in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of GNN and graph learning as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: 基于图神经网络的自适应量子计算控制策略
abstract: Quantum computing offers unprecedented computational power, but current control strategies often struggle with the inherent complexity of quantum systems. This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum computing control – a deep learning-based graph neural network (GNN) model – designed to adaptively control quantum systems. We propose a system where the GNN learns a representation of the quantum system's internal graph structure, allowing for dynamic adjustments to control parameters. This approach significantly enhances the robustness and efficiency of quantum computations. The core mechanism involves constructing a dynamic graph representing the quantum state, and training the GNN to optimize the system's evolution within this graph. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method through simulations and preliminary experiments, showcasing improved control stability and enhanced quantum computation efficiency compared to traditional approaches.

title: Adaptive Self-Organizing Network Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive self-organizing network optimization algorithm designed to address the challenges of dynamic environments and network adaptation. Traditional network optimization methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their adaptability. Our proposed algorithm leverages a self-organizing network structure and employs a novel learning mechanism to dynamically adjust network weights, thereby enhancing network resilience and performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and analysis, showcasing improved adaptability and stability compared to existing optimization techniques. The core mechanism focuses on continuous, incremental weight adjustments based on observed network dynamics, facilitating a robust and responsive network.

title: Dynamically Adaptive Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a cornerstone technology for building fault-tolerant quantum computers. However, traditional QEC schemes often suffer from computational inefficiencies, particularly when dealing with varying error rates across different quantum circuits. This paper introduces a dynamically adaptive QEC method that leverages machine learning to optimize the error correction strategy in real-time. The core idea involves predicting error probabilities using a machine learning model and then adjusting the applied error correction code based on these predictions. This approach promises to significantly improve the efficiency and robustness of QEC, addressing a critical bottleneck in the development of practical quantum computers. The method's efficacy hinges on the ability of the machine learning model to accurately capture the complex error dynamics within a quantum circuit. We present a framework for implementing this dynamic adaptation, outlining the key components and potential challenges.

title: Dynamic Quantum Topology Structures
abstract: The pursuit of efficient quantum computation necessitates the exploration of novel approaches to quantum state manipulation and control. This research investigates the application of dynamic quantum topology structures, proposing a system capable of dynamically adapting quantum topology based on environmental changes. title: String Theory Quantum State Dynamic Adjustment
abstract: This paper explores a novel dynamic adjustment mechanism for quantum states, leveraging the principles of string theory and the string-Hilbert relationship. The core aim is to develop a system capable of automatically adapting quantum states to environmental changes, thereby enhancing the efficiency of quantum computation. We propose a "quantum state graph" model that utilizes this dynamic adjustment to optimize quantum properties through quantum entanglement. This approach addresses limitations of traditional quantum computing, offering the potential for a more versatile and efficient quantum technology.

title: Neuro-Morphic Quantum Computing: A Hardware Architecture Exploration
abstract: This paper explores a novel hardware architecture for neuro-morphic quantum computing, aiming to leverage the strengths of both quantum and neuromorphic computing paradigms for enhanced parallel processing. The proposed architecture integrates quantum bits (qubits) with a neural network, utilizing the inherent parallelism of quantum computation and the adaptive learning capabilities of neuromorphic systems. This work outlines the core design principles and theoretical foundations, focusing on the efficient interaction between these two distinct computational modalities. The architecture's potential to significantly improve computational efficiency and scalability is discussed. The key elements include a quantum processing unit (QPU) coupled to a spiking neural network (SNN) via a carefully designed interface. The theoretical framework examines the impact of quantum entanglement and neural network plasticity on the overall computation. Further research directions are proposed to refine and validate this architecture.

title: On Simulated Annealing for the Solution of Differential Equations
abstract: This paper investigates the application of simulated annealing (SA) to the solution of differential equations. Traditional numerical methods for solving differential equations often face challenges in terms of computational cost, especially for complex equations or high-dimensional systems. We propose a novel approach where the differential equation solving process is formulated as an optimization problem, amenable to the iterative search capabilities of the SA algorithm. The core idea involves representing potential solutions as configurations within the SA search space and utilizing the temperature schedule to balance exploration and exploitation. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis and conceptual examples, the potential of SA to efficiently and accurately solve various types of differential equations. The effectiveness of this approach is primarily focused on the algorithmic strategy rather than specific numerical implementations, aiming to establish a fundamental framework for further research and development. The key contribution lies in providing a new method for solving differential equations by leveraging the strengths of simulated annealing. ---

title: Neural Symbolic Artificial Intelligence for Dynamic Knowledge Graph Fusion
abstract: This paper explores the application of neural symbolic artificial intelligence (NSAI) for dynamic knowledge graph fusion, aiming to enhance knowledge reasoning and decision-making processes. Traditional knowledge graph approaches often struggle with the inherent dynamism of real-world information and the need for flexible reasoning. We propose a novel framework that integrates the strengths of deep learning and symbolic reasoning, constructing an NSAI model capable of dynamically merging and utilizing knowledge graphs. The core mechanism involves leveraging deep learning for feature extraction and representation learning from unstructured data, while employing symbolic reasoning techniques to perform logical inference and deduction based on the fused knowledge graph. This approach allows for more adaptable and efficient knowledge representation and reasoning compared to static knowledge graph systems. The paper outlines the key components of this framework and discusses its potential impact across diverse applications, emphasizing the importance of dynamic knowledge integration for robust AI systems. We demonstrate the theoretical advantages and propose a foundational approach for future research in this area.

title: Non-Linear Temporal Logic Circuits
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to circuit design centered around the direct implementation of non-linear temporal logic (NTL) expressions. Currently, NTL reasoning often relies on symbolic manipulation and representation, introducing computational overhead and potential latency issues, particularly in real-time applications. The core idea presented here is the construction of circuits that bypass these symbolic steps by directly executing the operations inherent in NTL. This is achieved through the strategic use of feedback loops and switching elements within the circuit architecture, effectively translating NTL formulas into hardware operations. We demonstrate that this approach offers a promising avenue for high-performance reasoning, potentially exceeding the capabilities of traditional symbolic methods. The paper focuses on the theoretical framework and design principles, omitting experimental validation. The key contribution is the foundational concept and a detailed description of the circuit design methodology.

title: 基于自适应的遗传算法的优化策略
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization strategy based on an adaptive genetic algorithm (AGA). Traditional genetic algorithms often suffer from static parameter settings, limiting their effectiveness. This work proposes a dynamic adjustment mechanism that utilizes learned data to dynamically adjust optimization parameters, resulting in improved algorithm efficiency and quality. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this adaptive approach through a series of illustrative examples, highlighting its superior performance compared to traditional methods in various optimization tasks. The core mechanism involves learning a data distribution and adapting the optimization process accordingly.

title: 基于多模态数据流的程序形式化验证
abstract: Program formal verification aims to provide mathematical guarantees about the correctness of software systems. However, existing formal verification techniques often rely heavily on code, requiring significant manual effort to translate requirements and specifications into formal models. This paper proposes a novel approach based on multi-modal data streams to automate and scale program formal verification. We construct a data stream incorporating code, documentation, and test cases, leveraging natural language processing (NLP), machine learning (ML), and formal verification techniques to translate this diverse input into a formal representation suitable for verification. Our approach addresses the limitations of traditional methods by effectively utilizing auxiliary information, leading to more comprehensive and accurate verification results. We explore the core claim of automating and scaling program formal verification through multi-modal data streams and outline the core mechanism of transforming these data streams into formal representations using NLP, ML and formal verification tools. This work represents a significant advancement in the field by broadening the scope of formal verification beyond solely code-based approaches.

title: Разработка и анализ архитектуры модуля для многоуровневой верификации тестовых артефактов в отраслях промышленности на основе системного подхода
abstract: Данная работа посвящена разработке и анализу архитектуры программного модуля многоуровневой верификации русскоязычных текстовых артефактов промышленного назначения. Разрабатываемый подход ориентирован на проверку документов с учетом их типа, канала распространения, профессиональной терминологии, употребления англицизмов и изменений языковой и нормативной базы. Задачи, которые решались в ходе исследования: 1. Систематизация научных, патентных и программных источников, обоснование границ исследования и выявление требований к архитектуре модуля. 2. Разработка методологии многоуровневой верификации, включающей алгоритмы классификации документа, интерпретации англицизмов и адаптивной орфографической проверки. 3. Апробация разработанной методологии на реальных текстовых артефактах, проведение сценарного тестирования существующих сервисов и формирование рекомендаций по созданию единого модуля верификации. Работа проведена на основе системного подхода, при котором модуль верификации рассматривается как часть информационной среды предприятия. Для апробации предложенных алгоритмов выполнен ручной экспертный анализ пяти документов различного типа и функционального назначения. Проведено сценарное тестирование шести веб-сервисов: АЙNET, NormaSlov, ГосСловарь, AdSea, SenDev и ТекстКонтроль. Проведён анализ результатов апробации и сценарного тестирования. Установлено, что наиболее высокие значения интегральной оценки функциональной полноты получили ГосСловарь и ТекстКонтроль, однако ни одно из рассмотренных решений не достигло уровня, достаточного для промышленной эксплуатации без привлечения эксперта. На основании анализа обоснована необходимость создания единого модуля, объединяющего классификацию документов, обработку англицизмов, адаптивную орфографическую проверку и экспертную проверку неоднозначных случаев. Для достижения данных результатов в работе использованы следующие информационные технологии: Microsoft Word; pymorphy3 со словарями OpenCorpora; Natasha (razdel); АЙNET, NormaSlov, ГосСловарь, AdSea, SenDev, ТекстКонтроль; NLP, OCR, RAG и API.

title: Corporate-Family Resolution Is Not a String-Matching Problem: A Public Benchmark Stratified by Name Visibility
abstract: Deciding whether two supplier records belong to the same corporate family is a prerequisite for spend consolidation, credit exposure aggregation and sanctions screening. It is usually treated as entity matching, but the tasks differ: a family link connects records that are deliberately different entities, and the evidence often appears in neither record. We introduce CorpFam, a public benchmark of 54,864 candidate pairs over 10,307 corporate families, derived from 6,638,350 US federal award records in which every supplier self-reports its ultimate parent to a government registry. Pairs are stratified by name visibility: whether the names are identical after normalisation, share a distinctive token, or share none. Because strata have positive rates from 10.2% to 97.3%, we report per-stratum recall, base-rate invariant, rather than F1, which is not. The strongest of 5 matchers recovers 100.0% of identical pairs and 4.2% of invisible ones; no method exceeds 4.7% on the latter. The failure begins before matching. Blocking decides which pairs a matcher sees, and we evaluate 7 schemes spanning phonetic keys, attribute keys that ignore the name, and semantic nearest neighbours. None reaches three percent on invisible pairs, and their union recovers 6.8%. 93.2% of these links never enter the candidate set, so no matching-stage improvement can reach them. The links are real: against SEC Exhibit 21 subsidiary schedules, which share no provenance with procurement registration, 64.2% of invisible links are corroborated, against 0.16% under permuted parents and 0.41% against the same parent's wrong exhibit: two unrelated nulls agreeing to within 0.25 points. Corporate-family resolution is a retrieval problem misfiled as a matching problem; the intervention point is candidate generation, not ranking. The benchmark, adjudication log, and code reproducing every number are released.

title: Information Density Imbalance in Visual Object Detection
abstract: In object detection, the number of instances is typically used to determine whether a dataset exhibits a long-tailed distribution, implicitly assuming that the model will perform poorly on categories with fewer instances. This assumption has led to extensive research on category bias in datasets with imbalanced instance numbers. However, even in datasets where instance numbers are relatively balanced, models still exhibit category bias, indicating that instance count alone cannot explain this phenomenon. In this work, we first introduce the concept and measurement of information density. We then observe a significant negative correlation between a category's information density and its accuracy, and we investigate how the training process impacts this relationship. Empirical studies suggest that information density imbalance may be a potential source of category bias. To preliminarily validate the potential of information density, we made simple improvements to three advanced object detection loss functions using this concept. Experiments on the Pascal VOC, COCO-LT, and LVIS datasets demonstrate that information density can significantly reduce model bias while effectively enhancing the overall performance of existing loss functions. This study provides a new perspective for understanding the generalized bias phenomenon in object detection models and offers new tools for designing fairer loss functions and training strategies.

title: Do Cantonese-Adapted Language Models Better Predict Cantonese Reading? A Cross-Model Eye-Tracking Evaluation
abstract: Information-theoretic measures derived from autoregressive language models are widely used to characterize the expectations that shape human reading, but whether language-variety-specific training improves such psycholinguistic alignment remains unclear. This question is still open for Cantonese, where recent NLP evaluations reported mixed benefits from Cantonese-specific training relative to Mandarin-oriented or general-purpose models. Using naturalistic Cantonese eye-tracking data, we compare two within-family adaptation contrasts: CKIP GPT-2 Tiny versus its lightly Cantonese-adapted JED351 derivative, and Qwen2.5-7B versus CantoneseLLM-7B, which underwent substantially more extensive Cantonese continued pretraining and instruction tuning. From each model, we derive lexical surprisal, POS surprisal, entropy before the target, and entropy reduction. Lexical surprisal and the joint four-metric model consistently favor CantoneseLLM-7B, followed by Qwen2.5-7B, CKIP, and JED351, whereas entropy reduction favors CKIP. These results suggest that more extensive Cantonese-specific training can be associated with stronger predictive fit, while model rankings also depend on the information-theoretic measure being evaluated.

title: 基于自适应的自适应动态图论系统
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic graph theory system based on adaptive learning principles. Traditional graph theory systems rely on static parameter settings, limiting their ability to adapt to varying input data characteristics. Our proposed system leverages adaptive learning algorithms to dynamically adjust graph parameters based on observed noise and uncertainty, resulting in enhanced prediction accuracy. This approach addresses a critical limitation of conventional methods, offering a significant improvement in predictive capability. The core mechanism centers on the system's ability to continuously refine parameter values through iterative adjustment driven by input data characteristics. We present a framework for implementing this adaptive system and demonstrate its effectiveness through simulated data analysis. The key contribution lies in the integration of an adaptive learning algorithm that adjusts the system's parameters in real-time.

title: Audio dataset for blind review manuscript
abstract: This archive contains a speech audio dataset for blind review. Total audio duration: 12 hours, 10500 utterances from 16 speakers (S001-S016) covering 161 closed-set English dive commands, recorded under underwater / laryngeal (throat-microphone) conditions. The compressed package dataset.zip includes: - all/: directory containing all WAV audio samples (16 kHz mono), organized as all/{batch}/{speaker}/{label}/segment_NNN.wav - metadata.csv: utterance-level metadata (file_name, speaker_id, label_id, text, split) - phrases.csv: the 161 canonical phrase transcriptions and an in-train flag - speaker_info.csv: speaker-level information (speaker_id, gender) - split_report.json: train/validation/test partition information This dataset is only for manuscript blind-review purposes.

title: Title: Non-Local Quantum Entanglement – Scalable Communication via Entangled Fields
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, promises revolutionary possibilities, particularly in the realm of communication. This paper explores the potential of utilizing entangled fields to transmit information faster than light – a concept long considered theoretical. We investigate a novel technique that aims to manipulate entangled fields to establish instantaneous communication without the need for physical movement of particles. The core claim is to demonstrate the feasibility of FTL communication through the inherent properties of non-local entanglement. We outline the underlying mechanism, analyze the potential challenges, and present preliminary results demonstrating the generation and manipulation of entangled fields, suggesting a pathway toward a new paradigm in quantum communication.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Neural Network Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize neural network optimization. We propose a novel algorithm, "Quantum Entanglement-Based Neural Network Optimization," that leverages the instantaneous correlations inherent in entangled states to accelerate training significantly. The core mechanism centers around the design of a specialized "纠缠神经元" network, utilizing quantum entanglement to expedite the learning process. This approach aims to overcome limitations imposed by classical optimization techniques, potentially leading to substantial improvements in model accuracy and training speed. The paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical foundation, and preliminary results, demonstrating the potential of quantum entanglement to enhance neural network optimization.

title: Relational Neural Networks for Knowledge Graph Completion with Reasoning
abstract: Knowledge graph completion (KGC) is a critical task in leveraging the vast amounts of structured information stored within knowledge graphs. Traditional relational neural networks (RNNs) have achieved significant success by learning patterns within the graph structure. However, they often struggle with complex relationships and inferential reasoning. This paper proposes a novel approach to KGC by extending RNNs with explicit reasoning modules. These modules are designed to perform logical inference and deduction, allowing the network to go beyond simple pattern matching and accurately predict missing links in the knowledge graph. We introduce a framework that integrates RNNs with reasoning capabilities, demonstrating improved performance in KGC tasks. The core claim is that existing RNNs primarily focus on pattern matching, and our work addresses this limitation by incorporating explicit reasoning. The key mechanism involves augmenting RNNs with modules capable of logical inference and deduction. This new approach significantly enhances the ability of the network to complete knowledge graphs effectively.

title: Neurodynamic Computation: Dynamic Time Warping and Adaptive Weight Updates
abstract: This paper investigates the application of dynamic time warping (DTW) and adaptive weight update mechanisms within the framework of neurodynamic computation. Traditional neurodynamic systems often struggle with the inherent complexities of real-world signals, particularly those exhibiting non-linearities and temporal variations. We propose a novel architecture that integrates DTW for signal alignment and adaptive weight adjustment based on a Markov chain model and gradient descent, aiming to enhance the system's ability to process time-varying, non-linear inputs effectively. The core claim is that neurodynamic hardware should incorporate these mechanisms. The proposed mechanism utilizes a Markov chain to simulate temporal signal changes, coupled with gradient descent to adaptively adjust synaptic weights between neurons, thereby improving computational efficiency and accuracy. The results demonstrate the potential of this integrated approach for robust signal processing in dynamic environments.

title: Predictive Maintenance using Federated Learning with Edge-Based Anomaly Detection
abstract: Predictive maintenance aims to anticipate equipment failures, minimizing downtime and maintenance costs. Traditional approaches often rely on centralized data collection, raising significant privacy concerns, particularly when dealing with sensitive sensor data from industrial equipment. This research proposes a novel framework that leverages the strengths of federated learning and edge-based anomaly detection to achieve robust and privacy-preserving predictive maintenance. The core idea is to train a predictive maintenance model collaboratively across multiple devices using federated learning, while simultaneously employing local anomaly detection models residing on edge devices to identify deviations from normal operation *before* data transmission. This approach reduces the amount of raw data sent to a central server, thereby mitigating privacy risks and potentially improving model accuracy through localized anomaly detection. The framework is designed to be scalable and adaptable to various industrial environments. We present a detailed discussion of the system architecture, the federated learning process, and the edge-based anomaly detection techniques. The proposed method offers a compelling solution for industries seeking to proactively manage equipment health while safeguarding sensitive data.

title: 基于自适应拓扑的量子信息保护
abstract: Quantum information protection is a critical area in the burgeoning field of quantum technologies, requiring robust mechanisms to safeguard information from eavesdropping and manipulation. Traditional methods often lack the adaptability needed to effectively defend against sophisticated attacks. This paper explores a novel approach leveraging self-adaptive topology – a fundamental concept in quantum mechanics – to design a robust quantum information protection system. We present a design that dynamically adjusts the quantum state to mitigate potential attacks, resulting in enhanced security and resilience. The core of this system involves the creation and manipulation of quantum states exhibiting self-similarity, allowing for the detection of subtle perturbations and the implementation of sophisticated security protocols. We detail the design of a quantum state evolution algorithm utilizing self-adaptive topology, culminating in a theoretical analysis of its security properties and practical implementation considerations. The core claim focuses on the ability to dynamically adapt quantum states to counter potential attacks, thereby offering a significant advancement in quantum information protection.

title: Predictive Coding with Recurrent Neural Networks and Temporal Contextualization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to predictive coding by integrating recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to explicitly model temporal context. Traditional predictive coding models struggle to effectively capture the dynamic and sequential nature of many real-world phenomena. Our framework addresses this limitation by augmenting the standard predictive coding architecture with RNNs, enabling the network to learn and utilize temporal dependencies between observations. This allows for more accurate predictions of future states, grounded in a rich understanding of the past. The core contribution lies in the temporal contextualization within the predictive coding framework, providing a more robust and adaptable model for predicting time-varying data. We posit that this approach significantly enhances the predictive capabilities of the network, leading to improved performance in tasks requiring temporal reasoning. The proposed model is theoretically grounded in predictive coding principles and demonstrates the potential for capturing complex temporal patterns.

title: Navigating Schema Drift: Orchestrating Agents and Schema Discovery for Robust, Domain-Specific Knowledge Graph Question Answering
abstract: Knowledge Graph Question Answering (KGQA) over Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly translates natural-language questions into SPARQL, yet most systems are statically optimized for a single benchmark and degrade abruptly under cross-domain transfer or schema evolution. We present HARP (Hybrid Agentic-Retrieval Pipeline), a KG-agnostic Text2SPARQL architecture that operates without task-specific fine-tuning. A meta-controller orchestrates a ReAct agent and an execution-validated, schema-guided fallback pipeline. Both paths are grounded by a runtime FAISS-indexed Schema-Discovery service that absorbs structural change by building temporary indices from live SPARQL probes. The system is evaluated across four heterogeneous KGs: DBpedia, a structurally complex Corporate dataset, and two versions of a proprietary railway metadata KG (TrackVideo). The v1 to v2 transition of TrackVideo represents radical schema refactoring, allowing us to test true schema-drift resilience. The hybrid architecture attains a highly consistent performance across all datasets, neutralizing the degradations typically caused by schema drift. A multi-model Quorum extension over heterogeneous LLM families further increases reliability, demonstrating that hybrid agentic retrieval with execution-validated routing is a highly viable paradigm for portable KGQA in production-grade settings.

title: Popularity-driven random walk graph convolutional networks
abstract: We introduce the popularity-driven random walk graph convolutional network (PDRW-GCN), a topology-aware graph neural network that incorporates degree-biased diffusion to exploit the heavy-tailed connectivity of scale-free networks. By incorporating a structural bias parameter, β , the model dynamically reweights neighborhood propagation based on node degree. We identify a topology-dependent diffusion transition in heterophilic graph learning: Sparse heterophilic networks benefit from hub-amplified transport ( β > 0 ), whereas dense heterophilic networks require hub-suppressed diffusion ( β < 0 ) to prevent noisy neighborhood overmixing. Experiments across homophilic and heterophilic benchmark networks demonstrate consistent improvements in node classification performance measured by F1 score and receiver operating characteristic—area under the curve. Moreover, the model exhibits diminishing performance gains on non-scale-free topologies, indicating that β acts primarily as a topology-dependent routing mechanism rather than a generic regularizer.

title: Beyond Blur: A Semantic Tri-view Pipeline for Teledermatology Gradability via Skin Micro-relief
abstract: Smartphone skin photographs are indispensable to teledermatology, yet assessing the diagnostic suitability of submitted cases (gradability) remains a critical bottleneck in mobile care workflows. Dermatologists routinely review multiple photographic views (regional, angled, and close-up) to identify consistent textural detail rather than relying on a single image. We present the Semantic Tri-view Pipeline, an interpretable architecture for automated teledermatology gradability screening that formalizes epidermal micro-relief as a computable biomarker of image quality. Using an expert-annotated subset of the public SCIN dataset, we train a lightweight DeepLabV3+ model to segment micro-relief fidelity. These spatial masks are then aggregated across up to three case views with a logistic regression classifier, leveraging viewpoint redundancy to support robustness under uncontrolled smartphone acquisition. This approach learns context-aware, clinically intelligible heuristics, such as penalizing high-fidelity texture in regional distance views. Evaluated at a predefined 90% sensitivity operating point, the system's apparent errors largely reflect subjective clinical variance on borderline cases where clinicians rely on non-visual metadata. On SCIN, performance improves from an AUC of 0.81 (80.6% PPV) on variance-heavy majority-consensus cases to 0.96 (97.7% PPV) on optically unambiguous unanimous cases. Overall, this work delivers an interpretable, privacy-by-design, edge-ready system that can provide real-time feedback during case submission to filter ungradable photo sets before review.

title: Characterizing Text Branch Sensitivity in Medical Vision-Language Segmentation via Evidence Decoupling
abstract: Pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) have shown promising performance in medical image segmentation by incorporating clinical text. However, it remains unclear how much textual information actually contributes to pixel-level predictions. In this work, we systematically investigate the role of text in multimodal medical image segmentation. We first analyze several commonly used fusion strategies and find that segmentation performance is largely insensitive to the choice of fusion module. To further understand modality interactions, we propose an Evidence Decoupling Decoder (EDD) based on evidential deep learning and deep supervision. EDD serves as an internal representation analysis tool that decomposes image evidence and text-modulated evidence throughout the decoding process while maintaining competitive segmentation performance. Experimental results show that the sensitivity to text perturbation varies substantially across datasets. On BUSI and BTMRI, removing text causes catastrophic performance drops, indicating strong model reliance on textual input. On ISIC and Kvasir-SEG, text exerts relatively marginal influence. We further find that text affects predictions mainly through global semantic modulation rather than independent spatial localization, and that the specific semantic components driving text sensitivity differ across datasets. These findings provide a deeper understanding of modality interaction in multimodal medical image segmentation and offer practical insights for future model design.

title: GenCAR: Generative Counterfactual Alignment with Risk-Controlled Selection for Out-of-Distribution Recommendation
abstract: Serving useful recommendations under distribution shift is crucial for balancing utility and risk in out-of-distribution (OOD) recommendation. However, most existing OOD methods improve ranking or construct counterfactual candidates without controlling the proxy-label false discovery rate (FDR) of the served set. In this work, we formulate OOD serving as the $α$-Valid Counterfactual Recommendation ($α$-VCR) problem to retain candidate support learned from counterfactual supervision while controlling proxy-label FDR, and propose GenCAR, which couples preference-grounded counterfactual supervision with calibrated set selection. In particular, GenCAR fixes the stable-preference representation while intervening on the environmental factor, grounds offline large language model proposals through preference anchors and trust-radius filtering, and uses conformal $p$-values for Benjamini--Hochberg selection. We theoretically bound conditional counterfactual approximation error and prove finite-sample, distribution-free control of proxy-label FDR under exchangeability and positive regression dependence, with a Benjamini--Yekutieli guarantee under arbitrary dependence. Extensive experiments audit realized proxy false discovery proportions and demonstrate that GenCAR consistently enhances OOD candidate recovery across diverse benchmarks.

title: Old Search Trees, New Fruits: A State of the Art Review of AI Planning and Classical Search Revisited
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of AI Planning and Classical Search Revisited in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of planning and search algorithms as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Adaptive Microscopic Quantum Computing Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the potential of incorporating adaptive geometric optimization into the design and operation of micro-quantum computers. The core claim is that a novel framework leverages quantum entanglement and dynamically adjusted geometric transformations to optimize the state of quantum systems, ultimately leading to enhanced computational efficiency and precision. We investigate the fundamental principles behind this approach, detailing the design of the optimization algorithm and its application to a specific quantum system. The study explores how the interplay of quantum entanglement and geometric manipulation can provide a pathway to significantly improve the performance of quantum computations.

title: Topological Adaptive Quantum State Generation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum state generation algorithm based on topological adaptive principles. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the quantum state to accommodate complex topological structures, allowing for the generation of quantum states with intricate topology. The core mechanism centers around utilizing topological self-adaptation to evolve the quantum state, enabling a deeper understanding of the state's dynamics through the lens of topology. This approach offers a unique pathway to generate states with intricate topologies, potentially unlocking new functionalities in quantum information processing. The paper details the algorithm's design, analysis, and preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this technique in generating complex topological quantum states.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Generative Models with Uncertainty Propagation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to probabilistic programming focused on enhancing the handling of uncertainty within generative models. Current probabilistic programming languages often struggle with efficiently propagating uncertainty, particularly in complex hierarchical models. We introduce a specialized probabilistic programming language designed with native support for hierarchical uncertainty modeling and optimized Monte Carlo simulation. This allows for accurate uncertainty propagation during both model inference and generation. The core of this work lies in developing a more intuitive and computationally efficient framework for representing and manipulating uncertainty, directly addressing a significant bottleneck in the field. We outline the key features of this language, emphasizing its design choices geared toward streamlining uncertainty propagation. The results demonstrate a substantial improvement in the ability to build and utilize sophisticated generative models that accurately capture and represent uncertainty, ultimately leading to more robust and reliable results.

title: Quantum Bio-Inspired Computing (QBIC)
abstract: This paper introduces Quantum Bio-Inspired Computing (QBIC), a novel computational paradigm that leverages the inherent parallelism of biological neural networks to construct efficient quantum computing architectures. QBIC's core claim is that by simulating the complex, parallel processing capabilities of biological neural networks, we can build quantum computing systems capable of exceeding the limitations of traditional quantum algorithms. The central mechanism involves designing quantum neuron models based on quantum decoherence and entanglement, utilizing quantum circuits to emulate synaptic connections and inter-neuronal communication within biological neural networks, thereby enabling large-scale parallel computations. Unlike traditional approaches that directly implement quantum algorithms, QBIC represents a fundamentally new approach, drawing inspiration from biological computation and integrating it with quantum technologies. This offers the potential to tackle unstructured and complex datasets with unprecedented efficiency. The framework presented here provides a foundational approach for exploring the intersection of biology and quantum computing, potentially unlocking new computational frontiers. ---

title: Quantum Communication Protocol Design Based on Quantum Error-Correcting Codes
abstract: This paper presents the design of a communication protocol leveraging quantum error-correcting codes to enhance the reliability of quantum communication. The core idea revolves around encoding quantum information using a specific quantum error-correcting code and subsequently transmitting this encoded information. During transmission, the protocol employs error detection and correction techniques based on the chosen code to mitigate the detrimental effects of noise and decoherence, which are inherent challenges in quantum communication. The proposed protocol aims to significantly improve the robustness of quantum communication channels, a critical step towards realizing practical quantum networks and secure quantum key distribution. The theoretical framework and mathematical formulation of the protocol are presented, detailing the encoding process, error detection, and correction mechanisms. This work contributes to the growing field of quantum communication by providing a concrete design methodology for building more reliable quantum communication systems.

title: Core Claim: Develop a framework based on self-adaptive quantum system time exponents to simulate the time behavior of complex quantum systems using inherent self-correlation, allowing for automated parameter adjustment to achieve optimal prediction accuracy.
abstract: Quantum systems exhibit inherently complex and time-dependent behaviors, posing significant challenges for accurate modeling and simulation. Current time-index models often rely on approximations, limiting their ability to capture the true dynamics of these systems. This paper introduces a novel approach leveraging self-adaptive quantum system time exponents to address these limitations. We propose a framework that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on the system's inherent self-correlation, enabling automated parameter optimization for enhanced prediction accuracy. This method utilizes the system's self-adjoint nature to guide the model's evolution and improve the representation of time-dependent processes. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations of various quantum systems, showcasing superior predictive performance compared to traditional methods. This research contributes to the advancement of quantum simulation by providing a robust and automated tool for modeling complex time-dependent phenomena. The framework offers a fundamentally new perspective on time-index modeling, capitalizing on the unique properties of quantum systems.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Non-Local Data Dependency Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to deep learning leveraging the phenomenon of quantum entanglement for enhanced training efficiency and generalization capabilities. The core idea is to construct a neural network architecture where neurons are interconnected via entangled quantum states, enabling non-local data dependency learning. We introduce a framework where input data is encoded into quantum states, subjected to quantum gate transformations, and utilizes entanglement for information propagation. This fundamentally shifts the paradigm from classical, locally-connected networks to a system exploiting inherent quantum parallelism. The theoretical underpinning of this approach suggests potential advantages in terms of computational speed and model performance, offering a new direction for deep learning research. We explore the mathematical formalization of this process, emphasizing the key components and their relationships. The primary goal is to demonstrate the feasibility and potential benefits of integrating quantum mechanics into the architecture and training of deep neural networks. The exploration focuses on the design principles and initial mathematical framework for this entanglement-based learning system. ---

abstract: 数学をプロンプトとして利用するためには 数学を起動させるAIが必要になる。では数学を起動させるAIとは何か? つまり、偽AIアーキテクチャなのか最先端AIアーキテクチャなのかを判断できるのは AIを解読できるシンイチ数学が必要条件になってくるだろう。下記はChatGPT5.6による要約です。 本稿は、等速を x^N / y^N、変速を x^(sqrt(N) ± sqrt(y)) と表し、そこから等速中心と変速時に現れる意図成分を形式化する、派生理論の萌芽を生み出すための理論提唱論文である。等速では中心 C = x / y を観測できても、その背後の存在や意図を一意に特定できない一方、変速では基準からの符号付き残差によって状態変更の方向と大きさを記述する。 本研究では、シンイチ原論を理論基盤とし、それをAI上で作動させるために「方程式原理」を数学的OSとして用い、シンイチ原論を理論生成のソフトとして構成する。著者が命題や方程式を入力し、AIを実行環境として定義・公理・定理・証明へ展開することで、完成された唯一の理論を確定するのではなく、反例・再定義・拡張を含む後続理論を継続的に派生させることを目的とする。

title: Nonlinear Geometry Topology Analysis and Quantum Computing Coupling
abstract: This research explores the potential influence of quantum entanglement on geometric topology within quantum computing, proposing a novel quantum computation framework based on adaptive topology structures. The core mechanism involves introducing a dynamically adjustable topology structure, enabling continuous state evolution of quantum states and enhanced information security through quantum entanglement. Traditional quantum computing frameworks often rely on classical algorithms; this design leverages geometric topology as a foundational element, offering a potentially transformative computational paradigm. This work investigates the implications of this approach for stability, information protection, and overall quantum system design.

title: Quantum Entangled Matrix Encoding: A Dynamic Adaptation Strategy
abstract: Quantum Entangled Matrix Encoding (QEM) presents a novel approach to quantum computation by dynamically adjusting the encoding parameters of quantum matrices based on the underlying quantum properties. This dynamic adaptation is achieved through a specialized algorithm designed to leverage quantum phenomena like entanglement and superposition. The core mechanism hinges on a carefully constructed encoding scheme that evolves in response to these quantum effects. This research explores the potential of QEM to enhance quantum computation's efficiency and stability by intelligently tailoring the encoding process. This paper introduces a robust framework for QEM, detailing its theoretical foundation, implementation, and preliminary experimental validation.

title: Self-Referential Formal Verification of Quantum Circuits
abstract: Formal verification of quantum circuits is a crucial step towards building reliable quantum computers. However, the exponential scaling of quantum states makes traditional formal verification methods impractical for anything beyond small circuits. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging self-referential quantum circuits for verification. The core idea is to create a verification circuit that recursively simulates and verifies the behavior of the original circuit. This self-referential process allows for a more efficient exploration of the state space, mitigating the exponential growth problem. We define the key components of this system, including the self-referential circuit architecture and the underlying mathematical framework. The paper outlines the potential for this approach to overcome limitations of existing techniques and represents a significant advancement in the field of quantum verification. The primary mathematical challenge addressed is the efficient simulation of quantum circuits within a self-referential structure.

title: Neural Network Topology Adaptive Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm, the Neural Network Topology Adaptive Optimization Algorithm (NTAOA), designed to enhance the training efficiency and generalization ability of deep neural networks. The core of the algorithm lies in dynamically adapting the neural network topology by adjusting the connection strengths between neurons. This adaptation is driven by the local sensitivity of the neuron topology, resulting in an adaptive graph optimization strategy. The algorithm incorporates a regularization term based on the graph structure, further promoting stable and effective learning. Unlike existing optimization methods that primarily focus on individual neuron or weight updates, NTAOA leverages the global structure of the neural network topology, offering a more holistic and efficient approach to training. The key contributions of this work are the integration of graph-based optimization with neural network training and the development of a robust adaptive mechanism that responds to the evolving network topology during the learning process. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through theoretical analysis and conceptual demonstrations, highlighting its potential for significant improvements in deep learning tasks. ---

title: From Social Media to Generative AI: The Layering of Digital Mediation in Algerian Consumers’ Food Choices and Shopping Experiences
abstract: This study investigates the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in consumers’ food-related decision-making and its relationship with established social-media-mediated practices in e-commerce. A cross-sectional survey was conducted in Algeria in 2025 and generated 223 valid responses. 39.5% of respondents reported using AI, with ChatGPT making up 87.5% of applications reported by AI users. AI users experienced greater satisfaction with AI-related food experiences than non-users (Mann–Whitney U = 7,840.00, p < .001). However, AI use was not significantly associated with food purchasing after social-media exposure (p = .987). Social-media-mediated food discovery and purchasing practices remained prevalent, with no evidence of displacement by AI in the present sample. The findings conceptualize AI-assisted food choice as an additional layer of digital mediation in an established multi-source consumption environment and contribute evidence on AI-augmented consumer behavior to the under-researched Algerian context.

title: Discrete Gromov-Wasserstein Duality: Algorithms and Isomorphism Testing
abstract: The Gromov-Wasserstein (GW) distance provides a principled framework for aligning metric measure (mm) spaces based solely on their intrinsic structure. Its ability to identify isomorphic representations of distributions across spaces renders it valuable for comparing data where equality up to isomorphism occurs naturally such as in graphs or, more generally, distributions on graphs. Recently, a type of dual form for the GW distance between Euclidean distributions with the squared Euclidean or inner product costs was derived, spurring the development of new statistical and algorithmic results for this setting. This work furnishes a novel duality result for GW distances with and without entropic regularization that is applicable to all finitely supported mm spaces. Leveraging this result, we derive the sample complexity of empirical GW distances between finite mm spaces, as well as limit distributions under proper centering and scaling. Furthermore, we propose new algorithms for solving the regularized GW problem which are subject to formal convergence guarantees. These statistical and algorithmic advancements give rise to a principled and efficient framework for testing whether two distributions on the set of graphs with a fixed number of nodes are isomorphic based on samples.

title: Random-mapped intensity optical neural network: all-optical two-layer computing for multimodal optical-field inference
abstract: Free-space optical neural networks offer distinct advantages for computational imaging and machine vision because they can compute directly on incident optical fields. However, conventional ONNs composed of cascaded linear optical components are bound to a general linear input-output relation with square-law detection between the input field $\mathbf{x}$ and output score $\mathbf{y}$, $\mathbf{y}=|\mathbf{T}\mathbf{x}|^2$, where at best every complex-valued element of the transmission matrix $\mathbf{T}$ is trainable. This restricts each output score to a quadratic form $\mathbf{x}^\dagger\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}$ with rank-one decision matrix $\mathbf{A}=\mathbf{t}^\dagger\mathbf{t}$. Here, we present a random-mapped intensity optical neural network (RMI-ONN) as an all-optical two-layer computational network that lifts this rank-one limit. We numerically demonstrate that a high-dimensional feature projection by a disordered medium, a programmable nonnegative intensity mask, and segmented spatial power summation together can surpass the rank-one ceiling through the expressivity of higher-rank quadratic decision boundaries. Furthermore, exploiting the vectorial coherent wave-mixing nature of the disordered medium, we experimentally validate multimodal classification of amplitude, phase, and polarization on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and Quick Draw with the RMI-ONN, under a single optical configuration across all encoding domains. These results provide a practical and conceptual basis for scalable direct-field optical processors capable of exploiting amplitude, phase, and polarization information within a unified intensity-based inference framework.
