title: Dimension Dependent Correlation Gap Bounds under Restricted Independence
abstract: The pairwise independent correlation gap is the ratio of the maximum expected value of a set function under arbitrary dependence to that under pairwise independence, measuring the loss from this independence restriction. Under mutual independence, this gap is universally bounded by $e/(e-1)$ for monotone submodular functions. With pairwise independence, a tighter $4/3$ upper bound was established for several special cases, including $n=3$, and conjectured to hold universally. A recent AI-assisted counterexample disproved this conjecture for $n=5$, leaving the validity of the $n=4$ bound and the tight worst case bound open. We resolve both questions. First, for $n=4$, we establish that the $4/3$ bound holds universally and is tight using an AI-assisted proof combining theoretical analysis and computational verification. The proof combines a structural characterization of optimal numerator vertices, permutation symmetry, cone certificate systems, Bernstein polynomial representations, recursive simplex subdivision, and verification of $2,745$ Bernstein coefficient systems. Second, we show that the worst case pairwise independent correlation gap attains $e/(e-1)$ asymptotically by constructing an instance with identical marginal probabilities and a monotone submodular union coverage function on a ground set partitioned into $m$ blocks. The number of blocks grows sublinearly with the ground set size. The result follows by constructing a feasible solution to a scaled asymptotic reduced dual of the pairwise independent linear program and immediately extends to $t$-wise independent random elements ($t\ge2$), since $t$-wise independence implies pairwise independence. Thus, pairwise independence, despite being the least restrictive form of independence in the $t$-wise independence hierarchy, can be as restrictive as mutual independence in the worst case.

title: Optimal Fusion Strategies for Quantum Computation
abstract: Logical fusions are important for a number of tasks in quantum information, such as quantum error correction and quantum repeaters. In the photonic setting one must contend with the fact that physical fusions can fail, i.e. individual qubits are measured in a user-controlled product state basis with some probability, which can lead to a failure on the logical level. The choice of failure basis of each qubit is known as a fusion strategy, and finding good fusion strategies is important for optimizing performance of fusion-based quantum computation. Here we provide a complete characterization when $k=1$ qubits are encoded, and in particular characterize those codes and fusion strategies such that all but one physical fusion can fail, i.e.~\emph{perfect fusion strategies}. In doing so, we recover previously known perfect fusion strategies, and find perfect fusion strategies for quantum parity-check codes, answering an open question. We furthermore show that perfect fusion strategies are generic: random $[[n, 1, d]]$ graph codes admit a perfect fusion strategy with probability exponentially close to $1$. Additionally we motivate the study of a new graph parameter, namely the maximum degree of a graph at a given vertex taken over all LC-equivalent graphs, by giving a new operationally meaningful interpretation of it.

title: GeoSPRINT: Geometric Redundancy-Aware Step Pruning for Inference in Diffusion Trajectories
abstract: Diffusion models achieve high sample quality but remain expensive at inference time because sampling requires many sequential neural function evaluations (NFEs). Existing acceleration methods either use fixed step-skipping schedules, adapt step sizes based on local numerical error, or require additional training. We introduce GeoSPRINT (Geometric Step Pruning for Inference in Trajectories), a training-free framework for constructing non-uniform sampling schedules from the geometry of denoising trajectories. GeoSPRINT detects geometrically redundant steps using a hyperplanarity test in latent space, implemented efficiently via QR factorization, and converts the resulting redundancy profile into a sampling schedule that allocates more steps to high-curvature regions of the trajectory. In addition, we introduce the trajectory projection score $α_{\mathrm{traj}}$, a residual-variance metric that quantifies trajectory straightness and serves as a model-free diagnostic for rectified flow quality. Across CIFAR-10 ($32{\times}32$), LSUN Church ($256{\times}256$), and Stable Diffusion v1.5 ($512{\times}512$ latent), GeoSPRINT consistently improves over uniform DDIM (Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models) schedules at matched NFE budgets. On CIFAR-10, GeoSPRINT improves FID (Fréchet Inception Distance) by 0.7-1.1 over DDIM across 49-89 NFEs and surpasses DPM-Solver++ at NFE${\geq}30$ despite using a first-order DDIM solver. On LSUN Church, it reduces FID from 1.48 to 1.26 at 52 steps, and on Stable Diffusion v1.5 it achieves up to 1.93 FID improvement over DDIM. These results show that trajectory geometry provides a useful global signal for allocating inference steps and that schedule quality can substantially improve diffusion sampling efficiency without retraining.

title: Filtered quantum phase estimation
abstract: Abstract Accurate state preparation is a critical bottleneck in many quantum algorithms, particularly those for ground-state energy estimation. Even in fault-tolerant quantum computing, preparing a quantum state with sufficient overlap with the desired eigenstate remains a major challenge. To address this, we develop a unified cost-aware framework for filtered-state preparation that enhances the overlap of a given input state through spectral filtering. The framework covers polynomial and trigonometric realizations of filters and makes explicit the trade-off among overlap amplification, preparation success probability, and filter-implementation cost. As representative examples, we analyze Gaussian filters and introduce a modified Krylov-subspace-based filter that improves the success-probability/overlap trade-off relevant to filtered state preparation. Within this framework, we study a filtered variant of quantum phase estimation (FQPE) that mitigates the unfavorable dependence on the initial overlap present in standard quantum phase estimation. Numerical experiments on Fermi–Hubbard models show that FQPE reduces the total runtime by more than two orders of magnitude in the high-precision regime, with overlap amplification exceeding a factor of one hundred.

title: Formal Verification of Randomized Algorithms using Abstract Interpretation
abstract: Randomized algorithms, prevalent in diverse applications like cryptography, machine learning, and simulation, inherently introduce probabilistic behavior, posing significant challenges to traditional verification methods. This paper presents a novel approach to formally verifying these algorithms using abstract interpretation. We leverage abstract interpretation to create a simplified, abstract representation of the algorithm's execution, enabling the analysis of properties like expected runtime and correctness without explicitly dealing with the inherent randomness. Our methodology offers a more tractable framework for verification compared to traditional approaches. This work demonstrates the feasibility and potential of abstract interpretation as a tool for rigorous analysis of randomized algorithms, contributing to increased confidence in their reliability. The core idea is to approximate the algorithm's behavior with an abstract model and then apply verification techniques to this abstract model. This process allows us to identify potential issues before deployment and ensures adherence to desired specifications, even in the presence of random elements.

title: 基于多模态因果推理的智能代理
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to intelligent agent design centered around multimodal causal reasoning. Traditional approaches to agent intelligence often rely on correlation analysis, which can lead to spurious relationships and ultimately flawed decision-making. This work proposes a framework leveraging causal graphs and probabilistic inference to enable agents to understand and reason about the causal relationships between diverse data modalities – including text, images, and audio. The core claim is that an agent capable of understanding and reasoning about causal relationships will make more rational decisions. The proposed mechanism utilizes these graphs to model and traverse causal chains, allowing the agent to disentangle cause and effect and, consequently, to predict outcomes and take actions with greater accuracy and robustness. This approach represents a significant advancement beyond correlation-based models, establishing a foundation for truly intelligent agents that can operate effectively in complex, real-world environments.

This work proposes a framework leveraging causal graphs and probabilistic inference to enable agents to understand and reason about the causal relationships between diverse data modalities – including text, images, and audio. The core claim is that an agent capable of understanding and reasoning about causal relationships will make more rational decisions. The proposed mechanism utilizes these graphs to model and traverse causal chains, allowing the agent to disentangle cause and effect and, consequently, to predict outcomes and take actions with greater accuracy and robustness. This approach represents a significant advancement beyond correlation-based models, establishing a foundation for truly intelligent agents that can operate effectively in complex, real-world environments.

title: Quantum Computing Molecular Dynamics Simulation
abstract: Quantum Computing Molecular Dynamics Simulation aims to accelerate molecular dynamics simulations and enhance the ability to model complex molecular structures and interactions, ultimately providing more accurate molecular property predictions. This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum computing's unique characteristics to overcome limitations inherent in classical methods, resulting in significantly reduced computational complexity and improved simulation accuracy. We detail the core mechanism, focusing on how quantum algorithms can be employed to overcome the computational bottlenecks in molecular dynamics simulations.

title: 拓扑量子算法的自适应参数优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum algorithm optimization utilizing the principles of topological quantum algorithms. Traditional optimization methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the algorithm's adaptability. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts quantum system parameters based on the system's inherent topology, allowing for automated optimization and enhanced algorithm performance. The core mechanism involves constructing a topological representation of the quantum system and iteratively refining this representation to guide the algorithm towards optimal solutions. This approach offers a significant advancement in the field, addressing the limitations of conventional optimization techniques by leveraging the inherent properties of quantum systems. The work details the design of a robust parameter adjustment strategy and provides a preliminary assessment of its efficacy through theoretical analysis and simulated results.

title: Probabilistic Differential Equations for Complex System Dynamics
abstract: This paper investigates the application of probabilistic differential equations (PDEs) to model complex system dynamics, addressing the inherent uncertainties prevalent in systems like biological networks and climate models. The core claim is that representing dynamics through a set of probabilistic PDEs allows for a more accurate and nuanced understanding compared to traditional deterministic approaches. The proposed framework focuses on automatically deriving and solving stochastic differential equations (SDEs) from observed system trajectories, leveraging variational inference and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo methods. Unlike Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), this system actively learns the underlying differential equations, resulting in richer and more accurate models. This work contributes to a paradigm shift in complex systems modeling, emphasizing learning and adaptation over static parameterization. The theoretical foundation and algorithmic development are presented, outlining a novel approach to dynamic modeling that tackles the challenges of uncertainty and complexity.

title: Title: Self-Organizing Constraint Systems for Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the development of a novel self-organizing constraint system designed to enhance optimization algorithms. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with local optima, necessitating manual constraint adjustments. Our approach introduces a dynamically evolving constraint system that leverages the inherent structure of the optimization problem itself to automatically refine and avoid these suboptimal solutions. We propose a key mechanism centered around an iterative refinement process, wherein the system analyzes the problem's internal representation and adjusts constraints to guide the search towards a more globally optimal solution. The core aim is to automate the discovery of optimal solutions through a self-adaptive process, reducing the need for manual intervention and potentially leading to faster convergence and improved performance. This research focuses on the design and implementation of a system capable of adapting constraints in real-time based on the problem's characteristics. The paper details the architecture, the iterative refinement process, and the evaluation results demonstrating the effectiveness of this self-organizing constraint system.

title: 基于图论的自适应量子态生成与操控
abstract: Quantum state generation and manipulation is a fundamental challenge in quantum computing and quantum communication. Traditional approaches often rely on predefined quantum circuits, limiting the system's flexibility. This paper proposes a novel framework based on graph theory, specifically utilizing a graph-based quantum state model that dynamically adjusts the quantum state to achieve self-adaptive and complex quantum states. We introduce a novel algorithm for constructing and manipulating these graph-based quantum states, demonstrating its potential for enhancing quantum algorithms and communication protocols. The core mechanism hinges on the inherent properties of graph theory – self-organization, connectivity, and complexity – that facilitate the efficient generation and manipulation of quantum states. This research offers a new perspective on quantum state generation and offers a potential pathway toward more robust and versatile quantum systems.

title: Probability Algebra Neural Networks
abstract: Probability Algebra Neural Networks (PANNs) represent neural network parameters and learning rules as probability variables, employing probabilistic algebra operations for optimization. This novel approach aims to enhance generalization capabilities and model interpretability, addressing the limitations of traditional neural networks in handling uncertainty and complexity. The core mechanism involves transforming weights and biases into probability distributions, facilitating efficient optimization through probabilistic operations. This research explores the potential of PANNs to offer a more robust and explainable framework for complex models.

title: Adaptive Optimization for Complex Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the design and validation of an adaptive optimization system. The core focus is on developing a framework that dynamically adjusts optimization parameters based on the inherent characteristics of the problem. This adaptive approach aims to significantly improve optimization performance compared to static optimization methods. The proposed system employs a dynamic process, iteratively refining optimization parameters to achieve optimal results. This research will explore the effectiveness of this framework through rigorous evaluation and analysis of diverse problem types. The ultimate goal is to provide a robust and adaptable tool for tackling complex optimization challenges across various domains.

title: 基于自适应粒子的量子计算的计算范式
abstract: This paper explores a novel computational paradigm based on adaptive particles, offering a potential pathway to significantly enhance the efficiency of quantum computations. We propose a framework that leverages the inherent adaptability of quantum particles to mitigate the computational challenges inherent in many quantum algorithms. The core mechanism involves introducing a dynamic parameterization of quantum states, enabling the system to adapt to the problem at hand, thereby reducing the computational burden. This paper details the theoretical foundations, proposed algorithm, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the benefits of this approach. We highlight the potential for substantial improvements in quantum computation, particularly for complex problems demanding high fidelity and computational speed.

title: Dynamic Quantum Decoherence Control Theory and Quantum Defense
abstract: This paper presents a novel theoretical framework for dynamic control of quantum decoherence, specifically tailored for application within quantum communication and quantum computation defense mechanisms. The core of this work lies in the construction of a rigorous mathematical model of quantum decoherence, followed by the design of dynamic control algorithms utilizing established control theory principles. These algorithms are actively employed to suppress or manipulate decoherence, thereby bolstering the security of quantum information. We demonstrate a shift in perspective, framing decoherence control as a controllable systems problem, which provides a new approach to quantum defense. The theoretical foundations presented here offer a robust methodology for enhancing the resilience of quantum systems against environmental noise, a critical step towards practical, secure quantum technologies. Key areas explored include decoherence rate modeling, optimal control design, and adaptive control strategies. This research contributes significantly to the ongoing efforts in quantum information security and provides a practical roadmap for developing robust quantum defense protocols.

title: Adaptive Kernel Selection via Evolutionary Algorithms for Deep Learning
abstract: Deep learning models have achieved remarkable success across various domains, but their performance is often highly sensitive to the choice of kernel function. Manually selecting an appropriate kernel is a time-consuming and often suboptimal process. This paper proposes a novel approach to adaptively select and tune kernel functions during the training of deep neural networks using evolutionary algorithms. The algorithm dynamically evaluates different kernels on a small subset of the training data and iteratively evolves their parameters based on the observed reduction in loss. This adaptive process aims to identify and refine kernel configurations that maximize performance, ultimately leading to improved deep learning outcomes. The core claim is that automated kernel selection, leveraging evolutionary computation, offers a significantly more efficient and effective solution compared to manual selection.

title: 基于自适应的机器学习的图神经网络
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive machine learning techniques, specifically Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), to enhance the performance of machine learning models. Traditional GNN architectures often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to effectively adapt to diverse datasets and complex relationships. This work introduces a novel method leveraging the inherent self-adaptation capabilities of GNNs to dynamically adjust network parameters, resulting in improved model accuracy and generalization. The core mechanism focuses on a feedback loop that continuously fine-tunes the GNN's structure to optimize performance across a broader range of data characteristics. We evaluate the proposed approach on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate significant improvements in accuracy and robustness compared to baseline models. The results highlight the benefits of adaptive GNNs in enhancing machine learning capabilities.

title: Affine-Half Extensions of Partial-Spread Minimal Binary Linear Codes with Explicit Weight Distributions
abstract: In this paper, we derive complete weight distributions and solve constrained optimization problems for affine-half coordinate extensions of a known family of partial-spread minimal binary codes. The extended code has length 2m+2m−1−1 and dimension m+1, and it remains minimal. The repetition step and its preservation of minimality are elementary; the principal results instead consist of an affine Walsh-sum identity, exact translation incidence counts, and the resulting complete weight distributions when the affine normal lies inside or outside the union of the dual-spread components. The construction and weight distributions hold for 2≤r≤2t−1. In the principal range 2≤r≤2t−2, where m=2t, we characterize every optimal coordinate set for each prescribed extension size and solve the affine-half optimization exactly.

title: Emotion-Robust Speaker Recognition Through Synthetic Emotional Spectrogram Augmentation
abstract: Speaker recognition models are typically enrolled using neutral speech, yet real users rarely speak under emotionally neutral conditions. Emotion alters prosody, spectral structure, articulation, and speaking rate, shifting utterances away from the acoustic distribution observed during enrolment. Conventional augmentation with noise or speed variation introduces generic acoustic variability but does not explicitly model these coordinated, emotion-specific changes. This study therefore investigates whether synthetic emotional speech representations can improve speaker recognition when authentic emotional enrolment recordings are unavailable. Three conditional generative adversarial networks translate neutral mel spectrograms into angry, happy, and sad variants. The translation models are trained using lexically parallel neutral and emotional recordings from ESD and SAVEE. The generated spectrograms are subsequently added to neutral training data, while evaluation is conducted exclusively on genuine recordings from the independent RAVDESS and CREMA-D corpora. This protocol assesses whether learned emotional transformations transfer across speakers, lexical content, and recording conditions. Combined emotional augmentation improves speaker identification and verification on both corpora, with a larger effect on RAVDESS. Identification accuracy increases from 65.00% to 71.83% on RAVDESS and, by a smaller margin, from 56.04% to 60.20% on CREMA-D. The experiments further indicate that augmentation effectiveness depends on the target emotion and corpus, and that single-emotion augmentation can degrade recognition on some corpora.

title: Looking Things Up Before Speaking: A State of the Art Review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of RAG and retrieval as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: 基于非线性图的自适应机器学习算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning algorithm based on non-linear graph representations to achieve automatic parameter adjustment and self-adaptive learning capabilities. Traditional machine learning algorithms frequently require manual parameter tuning, limiting their adaptability. We propose a framework that leverages the inherent properties of non-linear graphs to dynamically adjust algorithm parameters, leading to improved performance and enhanced self-adaptation. The core mechanism of this algorithm involves constructing a graph representing the model's parameters and utilizing graph traversal techniques to optimize the parameters based on the observed data. This approach offers a more flexible and responsive learning process compared to traditional methods. We present a detailed implementation and evaluation of this algorithm on a range of benchmark datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving superior results through self-adaptation.

title: Machine Learning Prediction of Clinical Management Decisions from Referral Information in Child and Adolescent Psychiatry: A Temporal Transportability Study — Reproducibility Materials
abstract: This repository contains reproducibility materials supporting the study “Predicting Clinical Management Decisions from Referral Information in Child and Adolescent Psychiatry Consultations: A Temporal Transportability Study” The deposited materials include analysis code, the frozen clinical management coding framework, data dictionary, model specifications, aggregate analysis outputs, manuscript-aligned tables and figures, and synthetic/example data. No patient-level free-text clinical records or directly identifying information are included. Raw clinical records are not publicly shared because of privacy and ethical restrictions. The materials are intended to support transparency and reproducibility of the reported analyses and should not be interpreted as a clinical decision-support system or as containing data suitable for patient-level model redevelopment.

title: Automated Theorem Proving with Large Language Models and Symbolic Reasoning
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to automated theorem proving by integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) with traditional symbolic reasoning. Current automated theorem provers often struggle due to their dependence on meticulously designed, hand-crafted rules, limiting their adaptability and expressive power. Our proposed system aims to overcome these limitations by utilizing LLMs to generate potential theorems and then employing symbolic reasoning techniques to rigorously verify their validity. This hybrid architecture leverages the creative potential of LLMs while maintaining the precision and reliability of symbolic logic. We define key mathematical formalisms, including logical operators, and present a framework for a system that dynamically combines these elements. This work represents a significant step towards more flexible and robust automated theorem proving systems capable of tackling complex mathematical problems. The core of this approach is a feedback loop, where the verification process guides the LLM to refine its theorem generation, ultimately leading to a more efficient and accurate proof process.

title: Explainable AI via Causal Bayesian Networks and Counterfactual Analysis
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to explainable artificial intelligence (AI) utilizing causal Bayesian networks and counterfactual analysis. Traditional explainability methods often struggle to provide genuine insight into *why* an AI model made a specific decision, focusing instead on post-hoc feature importance. This work addresses this limitation by building a causal model that explicitly represents the relationships between input features and the AI's output. By leveraging counterfactual reasoning, we can then simulate alternative scenarios and determine what changes to the input would have led to a different outcome. The core of this approach lies in constructing a causal Bayesian network, allowing for the identification of causal pathways and a more robust understanding of the AI's decision-making process. We demonstrate the potential of this method through a theoretical framework and outline key considerations for its practical implementation. This research contributes to the growing field of explainable AI by offering a more transparent and reliable method for understanding and trusting AI systems.

title: Adaptive Self-Organized Computation for Quantum Key Distribution
abstract: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) utilizes quantum entanglement to establish secure communication channels, offering theoretically unbreakable encryption. However, practical implementations face challenges related to error rates and computational complexity. This paper proposes an innovative approach to QKD utilizing self-organizing quantum computation (SOC) to enhance key distribution efficiency and resilience. We demonstrate a novel SOC architecture that leverages entangled qubits to achieve faster computation and improved error correction, ultimately leading to a more secure and robust QKD protocol. The core mechanism centers around dynamically adjusting computational parameters to compensate for noise and errors, fostering a system capable of maintaining key integrity even under challenging environmental conditions. This research addresses existing limitations in QKD through the integration of self-organization, which promises a significant advancement in security and performance.

title: Quantum-Inspired Probability Distributions for Machine Learning
abstract: Quantum-inspired probability distributions are proposed as a novel approach to enhance the robustness and accuracy of machine learning algorithms. This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum-like phenomena, specifically superposition and entanglement, to mitigate the effects of noise and overfitting, resulting in improved model performance across a range of applications. We detail the core mechanism, outlining the design and implementation of a new distribution family centered around these principles. This work presents a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in several machine learning tasks. The core claim is that these distributions offer a significant advancement in robustness compared to traditional probability distributions.

title: Based on Biological Neural Networks: A Symbolic Reasoning Engine
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to symbolic reasoning by leveraging the inherent strengths of biological neural networks. Traditional symbolic reasoning engines often suffer from limitations in efficiency and interpretability, particularly when dealing with complex and dynamic knowledge bases. Our approach utilizes a mapping between symbolic logic rules and neuronal networks, employing synaptic plasticity to perform logical inference and knowledge representation. The core idea is to harness the massively parallel processing and pattern recognition capabilities of biological neural networks to create a more efficient and explainable reasoning system. We explore the feasibility of implementing logical rules directly within the structure of a neural network, capitalizing on the network's ability to learn and adapt through modifications in synaptic connections. This research suggests a potential paradigm shift in symbolic reasoning, moving towards systems that mimic the brain's ability to reason and learn. The architecture is designed to overcome the bottlenecks of traditional rule-based systems by distributing computation across interconnected neurons, leading to improved performance and enhanced interpretability.

title: Adaptive Probability Domain Modeling
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to domain modeling leveraging adaptive probability distributions, driven by reinforcement learning. Traditional domain modeling techniques often rely on static parameterization, limiting their ability to capture evolving relationships within data. Our proposed method dynamically adjusts the parameters of the domain probability distribution based on observed data and prediction errors. This adaptive process utilizes a reinforcement learning framework, where the model learns to optimize the distribution parameters to minimize prediction discrepancies. The core claim is that this dynamic adjustment significantly improves data analysis and prediction accuracy by better accommodating evolving patterns. The system observes data, calculates prediction errors, and modifies parameters like mean, variance, and covariance within the domain model. A reward function, based on prediction accuracy, guides the reinforcement learning algorithm. This work represents a significant advancement over static domain modeling approaches, offering a more robust and adaptable solution for complex data analysis scenarios.

title: Adaptive Geometry Parameter Adjustment
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to geometric model parameter adjustment, focusing on dynamically optimizing model performance through feedback. Traditional parameter adjustment methods often involve static, pre-defined adjustments, lacking the ability to effectively respond to real-time system data. We propose a dynamic adjustment strategy that iteratively adjusts model parameters based on performance feedback, aiming to achieve superior model accuracy and efficiency. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that continuously assesses model performance and adjusts parameters to minimize error. We present a theoretical framework and a practical implementation demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in a simulated environment. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in model accuracy compared to static parameter adjustment techniques.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel geometric optimization algorithm based on dynamically adapting random matrices. We detail the core mechanism of the algorithm, illustrating its ability to iteratively refine the data's spatial structure through the influence of the adaptive random matrices. The core claim is that this approach significantly improves the efficiency of data space optimization, particularly in scenarios with complex data distributions.

title: Anthropomorphism of Intelligent Chatbots in Conversational Influencer Marketing
abstract: The increasing integration of artificial intelligence in digital marketing has profoundly transformed the interactions between brands and consumers, particularly through the growing use of intelligent chatbots and influencer marketing. This study analyzes the influence of chatbot anthropomorphism on consumer purchase intention within a conversational influencer marketing framework. A quantitative survey has been conducted with 648 respondents and analyzed by structural equation modeling (AMOS). The results show that anthropomorphism has a significant positive effect on perceived congruence, social presence, and trust, which consequently stimulates purchase intention. However, it also elicits irritation, which negatively impacts purchase intention, thus confirming the ambivalent nature of anthropomorphism.

The results show that anthropomorphism has a significant positive effect on perceived congruence, social presence, and trust, which consequently stimulates purchase intention. However, it also elicits irritation, which negatively impacts purchase intention, thus confirming the ambivalent nature of anthropomorphism.

title: WinoQueer-NL: Assessing Bias in Dutch Language Models toward LGBTQ+ Identities
abstract: While English language models have been widely examined for anti-queer bias, Dutch models remain understudied. To address this gap, we developed a culturally and linguistically adapted Dutch dataset based on the English WinoQueer benchmark, containing pairs of stereotypical and counter-stereotypical sentences. To validate and expand it, we conducted an online survey with 43 Dutch queer participants, confirming 145 of 171 stereotypes as culturally relevant and identifying 22 new biases through free-text responses. The final released dataset, comprising 42,906 sentences, was evaluated using a range of Dutch-specific and multilingual models, including both masked language models (MLMs) and autoregressive language models (ARLMs), with bias measured via a score comparing log-likelihoods of stereotypical versus counter-stereotypical sentences. While the mean bias score across models appeared neutral (~50%), closer analysis revealed significant disparities: some models favored stereotypical sentences up to 97% of the time for transgender identities, but only 6% of the time for gay-related pairs, with transgender and non-binary identities consistently receiving the highest bias scores. Our findings highlight the importance of culturally grounded datasets for evaluating and mitigating biases that disproportionately impact marginalized groups in Dutch language models.

title: OBJECTION! Lawyer Agents Mitigate Guilty Bias in Legal Judgment Prediction
abstract: Legal Judgment Prediction (LJP) models are typically trained on documents that describe facts from a prosecutorial perspective. Existing datasets further exhibit severe label imbalance toward guilty outcomes. Consequently, these models suffer from "Guilty Bias", blindly accepting the prosecution's narrative as objective truth. Previous studies employing three-step reasoning structures or training on synthetically generated innocence data improve overall accuracy, but they still fail to mitigate bias at inference time. In this paper, we introduce OBJECTION, an inference-time pipeline that integrates an Adversarial Lawyer Agent into each 3-step reasoning of offense, unlawfulness, and culpability. Unlike generic critics, our agent actively challenges the model's presumptions of guilt by injecting legal defense arguments at each reasoning stage. To thoroughly evaluate this, we present a new "Natural Innocent" dataset including 3.4k real-world cases, overcoming the limitations of synthetic innocence benchmarks. Test results show that OBJECTION drastically reduces the False Guilty Rate (FGR) from 82.93% (SOTA baseline) to 16.69%, proving its capability to perform substantive legal reasoning. This work denotes a key progress toward aligning Legal AI with the presumption of innocence.

title: Spectra and kernels do not determine quantum steering
abstract: We show that the spectral data of a two-qubit state does not determine whether it isEinstein-Podolsky-Rosen steerable, already at rank three. On the slice of states withmaximally mixed marginal on the untrusted side - the normalized Choi states of qubitchannels - the two-qubit reduction/partial-transpose relation forces the partial-transposespectrum to be an affine image of the ordinary spectrum, so that isospectral pairs on thisslice are automatically iso-partial-transpose and have equal negativity. We then exhibit two exact pairs. The first is a one-parameter family of pairs with identicalspectra, identical partial-transpose spectra and equal negativity, one member of which isunsteerable for arbitrary POVMs while the other is two-way projectively steerable; thedifference lies entirely in whether the kernel is spanned by an entangled or a product vector.The second pair is stronger: two states sharing not merely the kernel type but the identicalkernel projector, the same spectrum, the same partial-transpose spectrum and the samenegativity, of which one carries an explicit local-hidden-state model for all projectivemeasurements with exact rational slack 7653/985000, while the other violates a three-settinglinear steering inequality with exact value sqrt(145156269/141610000). Consequently no function of the eigenvalues of rho and rho^{T_B} - including all moments,purity, entropies, rank and negativity - and no such function augmented by the full kernelprojector, can classify steering at rank three. As an application we exhibit an exactcounterexample, valid on a continuous interval of width 0.0116713828..., to the unrestrictedhigher-rank extension of a recently proposed Peres-type steering criterion; the provedWerner, pure-state and rank-two results of that criterion are untouched. The operativemissing coordinate is the orientation of the positive eigenspaces within the support relativeto the tensor-product structure. All stated constants are reproduced in exact arithmetic by the verification script includedin the deposit. The deposit also contains a claim ledger mapping every claim to its status,evidence and external dependency, and an explicit DOES_NOT_PROVE statement of scope limits. Certification note. Results were developed and independently re-derived across two separateautomated reasoning venues under a preregistration and dual-verification protocol, with everystated constant replayed in exact arithmetic in a second venue before inclusion. The depositincludes the replay script, its captured output, a machine-readable claim/dependency ledger,a clean build log, and SHA-256 checksums for every file. Scope. Theorem 2 and its corollary are unconditional, resting only on peer-reviewed criteria(Bowles-Hirsch-Quintino-Brunner, Phys. Rev. A 93, 022121 (2016); Cavalcanti-Jones-Wiseman-Reid,Phys. Rev. A 80, 032112 (2009)). Theorem 1 is conditional on two declared 2026 preprints(arXiv:2607.27757, arXiv:2605.21245) and is labelled as such in the manuscript.

title: Quantum Topologies: An Adaptive Computation Paradigm
abstract: Quantum Topologies (QT) offers a fundamentally new approach to computation by leveraging the inherent quantum properties of spacetime. This paper proposes a novel adaptive computation paradigm based on QT, where the computational structure is dynamically adjusted based on input data. We introduce a framework centered around quantum entanglement and a dynamically evolving topology, demonstrating its potential for complex calculations and predictive modeling. This work presents a conceptual framework and preliminary results, highlighting the unique capabilities of QT for addressing challenges in various computational domains. The core mechanism leverages entanglement to generate complex, self-organizing topological structures, enabling the computation of intricate patterns and relationships within data.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Error Mitigation for Complex Simulations
abstract: Quantum-enhanced error mitigation aims to improve the accuracy of complex simulations by leveraging quantum mechanics to detect and correct errors during computation. This paper explores a novel approach utilizing a quantum-inspired error correction algorithm to enhance the fidelity of results, offering a significant advancement over existing methods. We present a detailed mechanism, incorporating quantum-enhanced detection and correction, and discuss its potential impact on the field of complex simulations. The core claim is that this technique will dramatically improve the accuracy of simulations with inherent quantum noise.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: Probability Structure Optimization
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) holds significant promise for advancing artificial intelligence, leveraging the unique capabilities of quantum mechanics. A crucial aspect of QML is the optimization of quantum machine learning algorithms, and this paper proposes a novel approach centered around the integration of probability structure optimization. We argue that by strategically employing probability structure optimization, we can enhance the robustness and generalization capabilities of quantum machine learning models, particularly in the presence of noise. This research explores a specific mechanism involving the combined application of quantum machine learning algorithms and probabilistic structure optimization to improve the overall performance of quantum machine learning systems. The core claim is that this integration yields a substantial improvement in model accuracy and resilience against noise, representing a significant step towards practical QML applications.

title: Self-Correcting Neural Networks via Adversarial Training with Temporal Consistency Loss
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to enhancing the robustness of neural networks against adversarial attacks by incorporating a temporal consistency loss during adversarial training. Traditional adversarial training focuses primarily on minimizing the difference between the network's output for a clean input and its output after applying an adversarial perturbation. However, this approach often fails to address the issue of temporal vulnerability – the susceptibility of a network to adversarial attacks when presented with temporally shifted versions of the input. Our method addresses this limitation by adding a temporal consistency loss that explicitly penalizes changes in the network's output when the input is shifted in time. This results in a network that is not only resistant to immediate adversarial perturbations but also resilient to attacks that exploit temporal dependencies. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and illustrate its performance with a conceptual framework, highlighting the improved robustness compared to standard adversarial training. The core claim is that neural networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks that can disrupt their performance. The core mechanism is training a neural network with an adversarial training strategy, incorporating a temporal consistency loss that penalizes changes in the network's output when presented with temporally shifted inputs, enhancing robustness to adversarial perturbations. This work represents a new combination of techniques for achieving greater network resilience.

title: Symbolic Regression with Bayesian Uncertainty Quantification
abstract: Symbolic regression (SR) is a powerful technique for discovering mathematical equations from data. However, a significant limitation of traditional SR is its inability to effectively quantify the uncertainty associated with the learned equations and their parameters. This paper proposes a novel approach to SR that integrates Bayesian inference, enabling the estimation of confidence intervals for both the discovered mathematical expressions and their associated parameters. We introduce a framework where SR is performed within a Bayesian framework, allowing us to model the prior distributions of the parameters and the likelihood of the data given the equation. The resulting posterior distribution provides a comprehensive quantification of uncertainty. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and illustrate its capabilities with a simplified example. The core claim is that integrating Bayesian inference into SR significantly improves its ability to provide reliable and informative results by explicitly addressing the uncertainty inherent in the process. This work represents a crucial step towards more robust and trustworthy SR systems.

title: Composable Neural Program Synthesis with Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Neural program synthesis, the automated generation of neural networks from high-level specifications, holds immense potential for simplifying deep learning development and enabling new forms of AI. However, the complexity of neural network architectures and the vastness of the possible compositions pose a significant challenge. This work presents a novel approach to neural program synthesis leveraging reinforcement learning (RL). Our system employs an RL agent to learn the art of composing neural networks by selecting and connecting primitive operations (e.g., convolution, pooling, ReLU) from a predefined library. The agent's actions are guided by a reward function that directly optimizes the accuracy of the synthesized program on a given task. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach, showcasing its ability to generate reasonably accurate neural networks for various tasks. The core innovation lies in the integration of RL for guided exploration of the compositional space, offering a practical solution to the inherent difficulties of neural program synthesis. We define the problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and formalize the agent's learning process using RL algorithms. The system's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark datasets, highlighting its potential for automated neural network design.

title: Probability Geometry Algorithms: An Adaptive Optimization Approach
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic geometry algorithm leveraging the power of deep learning to automatically optimize geometric parameters crucial for complex physical models. We propose an adaptive optimization framework, integrating probabilistic geometry with neural networks, enabling the algorithm to dynamically adjust parameters to enhance the strength and stability of specific geometric structures. The core mechanism centers around training a deep neural network to learn the optimal parameters for each geometric configuration, facilitating automated parameter tuning and improved results. This approach offers a significant advancement over existing methods, particularly in scenarios requiring intricate geometric modeling and complex physics simulations. The paper demonstrates the effectiveness of this algorithm through illustrative examples and analysis, highlighting its potential to streamline the design and analysis of numerous physical systems.

title: Formal Semantic Network Reasoning Engine
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a formal semantic network reasoning engine. The core of the engine is built upon the principles of formal logic and automated reasoning, specifically utilizing Description Logics and ontology reasoning techniques. The system's primary function is to automatically construct knowledge chains from semantic networks and subsequently address complex data querying challenges. The key innovation lies in elevating semantic network inference to a logical level, resulting in more precise and reliable knowledge extraction and reasoning capabilities. This approach moves beyond traditional rule-based systems, offering a more robust and scalable solution for knowledge representation and inference. The engine utilizes a formalized knowledge graph derived from the semantic network, facilitating the application of automated reasoning mechanisms to derive new insights and answer intricate queries. The paper details the architecture, logical framework, and core mechanisms of the engine, demonstrating its potential for applications requiring sophisticated knowledge integration and reasoning.

title: Based on Differential Geometry: A Neural Network Architecture Design
abstract: This paper proposes a novel neural network architecture design rooted in the principles of differential geometry. The core idea is to treat the network's layered structure as a geometric space and leverage concepts such as curvature and tensors to guide the optimization process. Traditional neural network architecture design often relies heavily on empirical rules and heuristics, lacking the rigorous theoretical foundation provided by differential geometry. This approach aims to improve the network's ability to capture inherent geometric structures within data, potentially leading to enhanced performance in various tasks. We introduce a framework for constructing these geometric neural networks, outlining the key components and their mathematical formulation. The proposed architecture seeks to move beyond purely data-driven design, offering a more principled and potentially more effective method for neural network construction. ---

title: Information-Theoretic Graph Embedding for Anomaly Detection
abstract: Anomaly detection in complex networks, such as social networks, financial networks, and biological networks, is a critical task with widespread applications. Traditional anomaly detection methods often rely on statistical measures or graph-based approaches that may not fully capture the intricate information flow and dependencies within the network. This paper proposes a novel approach to anomaly detection based on information-theoretic graph embedding. We leverage information-theoretic metrics like mutual information (MI), transfer entropy (TE), and adjacency spectral embedding to learn graph embeddings that explicitly represent the underlying information structure of the network. These embeddings are then used to identify anomalies, which manifest as deviations from the expected information flow patterns. The core idea is that anomalies disrupt the normal information exchanges, and by embedding the network using information-theoretic measures, we can directly quantify and detect these disruptions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through theoretical analysis and provide a framework for further research in this area. The methodology presented offers a more robust and principled approach than existing methods, particularly in scenarios where the underlying structure of the network is complex and poorly understood. The key contributions are the integration of information theory into graph embedding and the development of a novel anomaly detection framework based on these embeddings.

title: Title: Self-Healing Modular Systems for Computational Models
abstract: The creation and maintenance of computational models is a complex and time-consuming process, often requiring significant manual intervention. This paper proposes a novel system, termed "Self-Healing Modular Systems," designed to automate this process, focusing on the creation and updating of models with built-in self-correction mechanisms. The core concept revolves around the implementation of a system of "mutation agents" that iteratively refine the model based on observed errors, guided by genetic algorithms. This approach aims to drastically improve the reliability of simulations by mitigating model degradation and facilitating continuous improvement. The system's effectiveness will be demonstrated through a focused investigation of model fidelity and stability.

title: 基于拓扑场的量子计算验证协议
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum computation verification protocol based on topological quantum structure. Traditional verification methods rely on static parameters, while this protocol leverages the dynamic adjustment of quantum computation's correctness to enhance its security. We present a framework demonstrating the potential for improved verification through the inherent robustness of topological quantum systems. The core mechanism involves constructing and analyzing topological quantum states to establish and validate the correctness of quantum algorithms. This approach offers a more adaptable and secure verification strategy compared to conventional methods. The research explores the practical implications of this protocol and highlights its potential impact on the robustness of quantum computation.

title: Neuromodulated state space models: a dopamine-inspired selective gating framework with memory–stability trade-offs
abstract: Dopamine shapes how the prefrontal cortex filters incoming information, maintains it in working memory, and releases it for action — three computational roles that closely parallel the input, state, and output stages of a sequence model. Here we ask whether formalizing this correspondence yields a sequence architecture that is both computationally competitive and mechanistically interpretable in biological terms. We introduce the Neuromodulated State Space Model (NeuSSM), which reinterprets the selective gating mechanism of modern state space models (e.g., Mamba) as three dopamine-inspired operators — sensory gating, working-memory modulation, and output relay — controlled by a single learnable gain parameter λ. We show theoretically that the classical S4 model arises as a limiting case of NeuSSM at λ = 0 (Theorem 1), and that NeuSSM’s local dynamical stability is governed by a phase-transition criterion based on the real part of the modulated state-transition eigenvalues, which partitions the model’s worst-case behavior into three qualitatively distinct regimes (Theorem 2). Mamba-style selective architectures are recovered qualitatively as λ → 1, though we present this correspondence empirically rather than as a formal approximation guarantee. Training NeuSSM on four long-range sequence benchmarks (≈ 0.45 M parameters, single consumer GPU), we find that the model learns different λ values in different layers depending on the task, with tasks requiring more flexible, long-range reasoning driving higher λ in upper layers — a pattern consistent with the proposed dynamical-stability trade-off (Theorem 2). NeuSSM reaches 98.75% on Sequential MNIST, 49.45% on LRA ListOps, 59.88% on Sequential CIFAR-10, and 76.0% on LRA Text, competitive with or approaching much larger S4 and Mamba baselines at a fraction of the parameter count. These results suggest that neuromodulatory principles from systems neuroscience can inform both the design and the interpretation of sequence models, even at modest computational scale.

title: A Data Fusion Framework for Grounding Aerospace Surrogate Model via Experimental Wind-Tunnel Observations
abstract: Aerodynamic surrogate models trained on high-fidelity CFD data reproduce numerical predictions of both scalar outputs and entire fields accurately, yet their predictive fidelity is limited by systematic discrepancies between CFD and experimental observations. We present an experimentally grounded correction framework that adapts a CFD-trained deep learning surrogate using wind-tunnel PSP measurements. A Geotransolver surrogate trained on 2,300 high-fidelity CFD simulations of the NASA CRM wing-body configuration, spanning geometric variation, Mach 0.70-0.85, and angles of attack 0 to 4 degrees, reproduces the CFD integrated aerodynamic forces and pitching moment to R2 > 0.99 but does not match the experimental data. To incorporate experimental information without retraining the surrogate, a correction network is trained on spatially registered PSP measurements at two freestream Mach numbers (0.70 and 0.85) across the same angle-of-attack range, learning the discrepancy between the surrogate-predicted and experimentally measured surface-pressure distributions. At Mach 0.85 the correction substantially improves agreement with PSP, particularly at the wing suction peak, shock location, and subsequent pressure recovery, reducing both the magnitude of the prediction error and the fraction of wetted surface on which it exceeds 0.05 in Cp, and it does so from a limited experimental dataset without modifying the pretrained surrogate parameters. On held-out angles of attack the grounded surrogate agrees with measurement to within 2.3-2.7% of the measured Cp range, and outperforms direct interpolation between the measured conditions at every state tested. Experimental measurements can therefore ground a large-scale simulation-trained surrogate by learning systematic CFD-to-experiment discrepancies while preserving its generalization capability and computational efficiency.

title: Loom: Weaving Diagnostic Strands into Free-Text Consensus via Embedding-Space Reweighting
abstract: Aggregating noisy, conflicting textual hypotheses into a reliable consensus is a fundamental challenge when deploying NLP systems in real-world industrial settings. While monolithic Large Language Model (LLM) agents offer unbounded expressivity for tasks like Root Cause Analysis (RCA), they suffer from context limits, compounding hallucinations, and prohibitive inference latency. Traditional weak supervision offers statistical rigor but is mathematically restricted to discrete classes. We present Loom, a generative consensus framework deployed for real-world RCA that bridges these paradigms. Loom aggregates open-form hypotheses emitted by modular heuristics (diagnostic templates dynamically populated with episode-specific entities, times, and metrics) by projecting them into a continuous embedding space, and resolves conflicting signals with an iterative centroid-based reweighting algorithm. The resulting consensus weights ground a single lightweight LLM synthesis step. Evaluated on the OpenRCA benchmark, Loom occupies the accuracy--efficiency Pareto frontier: it matches a state-of-the-art autonomous agent on Bank and Market-2 and trails on Market-1 and Telecom, while using a single LLM call per incident on all four datasets ($\sim$26$\times$ faster; $\sim$33$\times$ with an 8B-parameter synthesizer). We discuss our deployment experience, highlighting lessons learned regarding the trade-offs between agentic depth and inference latency, negative results in redundancy detection, and how deterministic consensus fosters trust among Subject Matter Experts~(SMEs).

title: Programming anharmonic potentials in a superconducting harmonic oscillator
abstract: Continuous-variable quantum systems offer a resource-efficient route to universal quantum information processing and analogue quantum simulation of real-world processes, such as molecular physics and chemical reactions. Realising these applications, however, requires non-Gaussian operations that implement anharmonic potentials, which are challenging to engineer on demand. Here, we demonstrate a systematic framework to implement programmable non-Gaussian phase gates $e^{-iV(\hat{X})}$, corresponding to the impulsive action of a potential $V(\hat{X})$, in a superconducting harmonic oscillator coupled to a transmon qubit. Using modular circuits derived from bosonic quantum signal processing, we realise a range of target anharmonic potentials on a single piece of hardware by varying a set of qubit rotations interleaved with a fixed calibrated control unitary. We first demonstrate a cubic phase gate, a key ingredient for universal quantum information processing. The resulting high-fidelity non-Gaussian states and the potential reconstructed using our pointwise force reconstruction method jointly confirm the cubic nature of the target gate. We then engineer a family of double-well potentials, relevant models of tunnelling and biased transfer processes, and experimentally validate the double-well topology and the tunable asymmetry. Finally, we engineer an approximate Morse gate, a step towards realistic potentials of molecular vibrational systems, and provide a concrete path towards high-quality engineering and reconstruction of the exponential form. Together, these results establish a practical and reconfigurable route towards continuous-variable quantum information processing and anharmonic quantum simulation.

title: TempoGround: State-Aware Streaming Visual Grounding with Vision-Language Models
abstract: Visual grounding maps language referents to spatial targets and is central to open-vocabulary perception with vision-language models. Existing methods have made substantial progress on single-frame and video-based visual grounding, yet under streaming inputs they still suffer from identity drift, cross-frame inconsistency, and fragile localization under partial occlusion. To address these issues, we present TempoGround, a VLM-native framework that detects cross-frame object correspondence and explicitly models object presence states, thereby enabling accurate and consistent visual grounding under streaming inputs. The key is a curriculum prediction mechanism guided by state-aware cross-frame correspondence: TempoGround resolves 2D instance association, predicts whether each object newly enters, continues in, or leaves the view, decodes the 2D box, and then lifts it to a camera-frame 3D box. As token-level supervision alone cannot capture the geometric objectives of streaming grounding, we further introduce Streaming Grounding Reinforcement (SGR), which optimizes TempoGround with verifiable Grounding, Identity, and Consistency rewards, jointly reinforcing persistent localization and temporally consistent predictions. We carefully design a three-stage training strategy and train TempoGround on large-scale data. We evaluate visual grounding under causally streaming inputs on multiple challenging benchmarks: TempoGround improves F1_2D@0.5 and F1_2D@0.95 by 4.4 and 0.5 on average, and F1_3D@0.25 and AP_3D by 6.2 and 7.5, respectively. These results demonstrate that TempoGround provides a practical foundation for visual grounding under streaming inputs.

title: Low-overhead tailoring and learning of noise in graph states
abstract: Graph and hypergraph states are important resource states for realizing universal quantum computation and diverse non-local physical phenomena. However, noise learning in such states is challenging due to their large entanglement and magic. This work establishes a low Clifford hierarchy circuit-based scheme for tailoring and learning noise in (hyper)graph states generated by multiple controlled-Z gates. The key is to convert the noisy input state into diagonal form and derive the convolution equation for the diagonal noise rates, which has a lower resource overhead. Such a diagonal form can be used in real quantum simulation by using the same conversion technique on the graph state input. We demonstrate that a single-depth Bell measurement is sufficient in our scheme for arbitrary graph states, while noise tailoring can be done via Pauli operations. After that, we suggest the Walsh-Hadamard transform and some approximation method for decoding the convolution equation to estimate the tailored noise. We prove that constant sampling and polynomial time complexities are sufficient to guarantee bounded noise estimation error with respect to the $l_2$-norm, which usually requires exponential complexity with existing noise estimation methods. The polynomial complexities are maintained even for the more stringent $l_1$ approximation under the sparse noise assumption. Conclusively, we propose novel methods for characterizing the noise properties of an entangled state at a lower cost than that of state generation. Moreover, compared with state verification methods, we can attain richer information on noise rates and enable noise mitigation, thereby providing guarantees for the preparation of graph states.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Feature Extraction
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to quantum data analysis, focusing on the automated extraction of key features through the application of a quantum algorithm. The core aim is to improve the efficiency of data processing by leveraging the inherent properties of quantum systems to identify subtle patterns and correlations within data. We introduce a novel system that dynamically adapts to the data's characteristics, ensuring optimal feature extraction for a wide range of quantum datasets. The system employs a quantum algorithm specifically designed for pattern recognition, resulting in a significantly enhanced analysis process. This research addresses a critical challenge in quantum data science – the need for efficient and automated feature discovery – offering a potential paradigm shift in data processing methodologies.

title: Quantum State Adaptive Computing: Towards Adaptive and Secure Quantum Computation
abstract: Quantum state adaptive computing represents a paradigm shift in quantum information processing, moving beyond traditional algorithms to leverage the inherent adaptability of quantum states. This paper explores the potential of this approach to design quantum algorithms and computation models that exhibit self-adaptation, crucial for addressing security vulnerabilities and enabling a wider range of applications. We introduce the core claim that utilizing quantum state adaptability allows for the creation of quantum computation systems with enhanced resilience and security. Our mechanism centers on strategically employing quantum information security algorithms to safeguard quantum information throughout its lifecycle. The paper details a novel design for adaptive quantum algorithms and computational models, emphasizing the crucial role of quantum state adaptability in achieving robust and secure quantum systems. The research explores the benefits and challenges of this approach, highlighting its potential impact on the future of quantum computing.

title: Formal Verification Program Generation (FVPG)
abstract: This paper explores the emerging field of Formal Verification Program Generation (FVPG), a novel approach to software development that leverages the power of formal verification techniques to automatically generate programs satisfying specified security and performance constraints. The core concept involves integrating formal verification methods with program generation methodologies. A verification engine is employed to generate program code segments that adhere to the established constraints, which are subsequently assembled into complete, functional programs. This approach offers a potential solution to the increasing complexity and criticality of software systems, where guaranteeing correctness and reliability is paramount. We outline the fundamental principles, potential challenges, and future directions of this rapidly developing area. The key contribution lies in the automated bridge between rigorous verification and practical program synthesis, opening avenues for developing demonstrably correct and efficient software.

title: Quantum Topology for Probabilistic Machine Learning
abstract: Quantum topology, a field of physics and mathematics, describes geometric structures that exhibit unusual properties of entanglement and non-locality. This paper explores the application of quantum topology to probabilistic machine learning, focusing on the design of a model leveraging quantum spin states and rotations to learn data distributions and predict outcomes. We propose a novel approach that utilizes the inherent quantum properties of spacetime to create a probabilistic model capable of enhanced prediction and classification. The core mechanism involves mapping data into a quantum state, allowing the model to exploit entanglement and superposition to achieve superior performance. This research addresses the limitations of traditional machine learning algorithms by introducing a fundamentally different approach based on quantum principles. The benefits include improved robustness, adaptability, and the potential for uncovering hidden patterns within complex data.

title: The Adaptive Quantum Algorithm Probability Model
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive quantum algorithm probability model, designed to enhance the optimization and stability of quantum algorithms. Traditional quantum algorithms often rely on static parameters, while this research focuses on probabilistic models, enabling efficient parameter tuning and improved performance. We present a framework for constructing probabilistic models that translate quantum algorithm execution into distribution functions, leveraging the inherent properties of probability to guide optimization. The core mechanism centers around exploiting quantum algorithms' unique characteristics to create a probabilistic representation of the computation, enabling targeted parameter adjustments to improve algorithm performance. The novel contribution lies in the integration of this probabilistic model into a robust optimization framework, addressing a critical challenge in the design and application of quantum algorithms.

The novel contribution lies in the integration of this probabilistic model into a robust optimization framework, addressing a critical challenge in the design and application of quantum algorithms.

title: Probabilistic Grammatical Inference with Bayesian Hidden Markov Models
abstract: This paper presents a novel Bayesian approach to probabilistic grammatical inference, specifically designed for learning context-free grammars (CFGs) from noisy and incomplete data. The core idea revolves around integrating Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) to model the underlying linguistic structures, effectively handling the inherent uncertainties present in real-world language data. We utilize variational inference to approximate the posterior distribution of the CFG parameters, with the HMMs providing a robust framework for representing and propagating uncertainty in transition probabilities. The resulting model offers a significant improvement over traditional CFG learning methods, particularly in scenarios where data is sparse, ambiguous, or contains significant noise. This approach provides a more robust and adaptable solution for language modeling tasks, addressing limitations of existing techniques by explicitly acknowledging and modeling uncertainty within the grammatical structure itself. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and a conceptual outline of its implementation, paving the way for future research and practical applications. ---

title: 基于量子退相干的通信协议优化
abstract: This paper investigates the optimization of quantum communication protocols leveraging the phenomenon of quantum decoherence. Traditional quantum communication protocols frequently rely on fixed parameter settings, often neglecting the dynamic influence of decoherence on channel performance. We propose a framework for dynamically adjusting protocol parameters based on real-time decoherence measurements. This framework aims to maximize communication efficiency and security by exploiting the controllable nature of decoherence. Specifically, we explore the relationship between interaction strength, decoherence time, and key protocol parameters such as pulse duration and detuning. The core claim is that by controlling these factors, optimal performance can be achieved. The proposed method offers a potential pathway to enhancing quantum communication robustness and scalability. Mathematical formulations are presented to quantify the impact of these parameters and guide the optimization process.

title: Looking Things Up Before Speaking: A Comparative Analysis Review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of RAG and retrieval as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Quantum Entanglement Computation via Dynamic Topology Simplification
abstract: Quantum entanglement remains a cornerstone of quantum computing, offering unparalleled computational capabilities. However, harnessing its full potential is hampered by the inherent computational complexity arising from entangled states. This paper presents a novel quantum entanglement computation framework, leveraging dynamic topology simplification (DTS) to dramatically reduce this complexity and enhance the efficiency of information storage and utilization. We propose a method to transform the complex entanglement landscape into a simplified, topologically driven structure, utilizing this structure to guide the computation and optimize information handling. The core claim is that this approach significantly lowers entanglement calculation complexity and improves the utilization of entangled information. This work explores the potential of DTS to unlock new computational avenues and address key limitations in quantum entanglement applications.

title: Quantum Neural Networks: Adaptive Activation for Enhanced Efficiency
abstract: Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) represent a paradigm shift in machine learning, leveraging the unique properties of quantum systems to potentially surpass classical neural networks. However, the inherent complexity of quantum systems presents significant challenges in designing efficient and adaptable architectures. This paper explores the integration of adaptive activation functions into QNNs to address this challenge. We propose a novel mechanism for dynamically adjusting activation function parameters, fostering increased efficiency and improved model performance. The core of our work lies in a system that employs a feedback loop, iteratively refining the activation function based on the network's internal state and the task at hand. This adaptive process significantly reduces computational costs compared to static activation functions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and preliminary experiments, showcasing enhanced performance in a targeted task. The resulting QNN exhibits superior results in terms of accuracy and speed, highlighting the potential of this novel activation mechanism.
