title: Neural Symbolic Causal Reasoning Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework, Neural Symbolic Causal Reasoning Networks (NSCRN), that integrates the strengths of neural networks and symbolic causal reasoning engines to achieve robust and interpretable modeling and prediction of complex system dynamics. The core idea is to build a hierarchical neural network where lower layers extract sensory data and patterns, while higher layers perform symbolic causal inference. This leverages graph structures to represent causal relationships and facilitates backward causal inference, guiding the activity of the neural network. Unlike existing methods that rely solely on neural or symbolic approaches, NSCRN combines these paradigms to offer enhanced reasoning capabilities, particularly in handling uncertainty and noise inherent in real-world systems. The framework addresses limitations of purely neural models in representing causality and purely symbolic models in dealing with noisy data. The primary contribution lies in the architecture and the integration of causal inference within a deep learning framework, leading to improved predictive accuracy and explainability. The system is designed to learn causal relationships directly from data while leveraging symbolic reasoning for precise and reliable inference. We demonstrate the potential of NSCRN through a conceptual framework, outlining the key components and their interactions.

title: ##基于多模态感知融合的自适应知识图谱构建
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to constructing and maintaining knowledge graphs (KGs) through multimodal perception fusion and adaptive reasoning. The core idea is to leverage diverse data modalities – including visual, auditory, and textual information – to autonomously build and dynamically update KGs. The system employs a multimodal perception module to transform these raw data into unified vector representations. An attention mechanism is then utilized to weigh the contributions of each modality based on its relevance and reliability. The fused information is subsequently integrated with a knowledge graph reasoning engine, facilitating tasks such as entity recognition, relation extraction, knowledge inference, and knowledge update. This approach overcomes the limitations of traditional KG construction methods, which heavily rely on manual annotation, resulting in increased coverage, accuracy, and adaptability of the knowledge graph. The system demonstrates the potential for real-time KG construction and dynamic updates in scenarios requiring continuous knowledge acquisition and refinement. ---

title: Efficient Abstractive Text Summarization with Large Language Models: A Focused Survey
abstract: Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have significantly improved the quality of abstractive text summarization. However, the high computational cost and memory requirements of these models limit their practical adoption, particularly in resource-constrained environments. This focused survey reviews recent progress in efficient LLM-based abstractive text summarization, emphasizing methods designed to operate under realistic hardware constraints. The survey first provides a concise background on abstractive and extreme summarization, highlighting challenges introduced by long contexts and aggressive compression. A structured taxonomy is then proposed to categorize existing approaches according to model architecture, training strategy, adaptation technique, and hardware awareness. Building on this taxonomy, the paper analyzes key efficiency-oriented techniques, including parameter-efficient fine-tuning, low-bit quantization, precision optimization, and inference-time acceleration. Furthermore, commonly used evaluation protocols are reviewed, emphasizing the limitations of traditional automated metrics and the growing need for faithfulness- and cost-aware evaluation. A comparative discussion summarizes trade-offs between summarization quality and computational efficiency, offering practical guidelines for model selection and deployment. Finally, open challenges and future research directions are outlined, including faithful extreme summarization, long-context processing, multimodal summarization, and standardized efficiency-aware benchmarks. Overall, this survey provides researchers and practitioners with a clear, structured overview of practical considerations for efficient LLM-based text summarization.

title: Multimodal collaborative modeling of teacher verbal and non-verbal classroom behaviors for teaching effectiveness prediction
abstract: Abstract Teacher classroom behavior sits at the centre of any serious attempt to understand and improve instructional quality, yet the verbal and the non-verbal channel are still typically examined apart, which leaves their pedagogically meaningful interdependence unmodelled. This paper proposes a multimodal deep learning framework that models the two channels collaboratively and predicts teaching effectiveness from their joint representation. Four modules compose the framework: temporal synchronization of the audio and video streams, parallel unimodal encoding through BERT-based language representation and SlowFast spatiotemporal networks, bidirectional cross-modal attention fusion regulated by a gated modality weighting mechanism, and a dual-head prediction network optimized jointly for effectiveness classification and continuous score regression. On a corpus of 186 classroom sessions recorded in 12 schools, the framework attains 82.3% classification accuracy, 80.1% macro-F1, an RMSE of 6.58 and a Pearson correlation of 0.879, ahead of ten comparison systems spanning unimodal, traditional machine learning and state-of-the-art multimodal fusion approaches. Ablation identifies bidirectional cross-modal attention as the component that matters most, and an attention analysis conducted across all test sessions indicates that verbal-gestural temporal synchrony accompanies higher observer-rated teaching effectiveness. The framework thus offers a scalable, automated route from multimodal teacher behavior to instructional outcomes, with potential applications in teacher professional development and intelligent classroom observation systems.

title: Differentiable Electricity-Market Clearing for Gradient-Based Planning
abstract: Planning a large data center is difficult because a facility big enough to matter changes the electricity prices it will pay. Those prices are set by market clearing, a constrained optimization problem solved anew in every operating condition. However, simulating the market tells a planner how a candidate plan performs but not how to improve it. Here we treat market clearing as a differentiable optimization layer: each forward pass solves the market, and reverse-mode automatic differentiation propagates the planning cost back through the cleared prices to the plan. After validating these gradients against finite differences, we apply them to a concrete problem: allocating 50 MW of data-center load across six candidate buses in two synthetic networks, under a fixed cost per active site, evaluated over 36 operating states. Judged against exhaustive enumeration of all site combinations, gradient optimization recovers the continuous allocations almost exactly, with worst-case objective gaps of 2.3\% and 8.5\% of the cost difference between the best and worst single site. Its one systematic error is instructive: near the costs at which a site should close, the smooth relaxation of the discrete site count shrinks the site rather than closing it, so discrete transitions arrive late. Differentiable market clearing thus turns market-aware planning into a problem gradients can search.

title: Counterfactual Behavior Cloning: Offline Imitation Learning from Imperfect Human Demonstrations
abstract: Learning from humans is challenging because people are imperfect teachers. When everyday humans show the robot a new task they want it to perform, humans inevitably make errors (e.g., inputting noisy actions) and provide suboptimal examples (e.g., overshooting the goal). Existing methods often learn by matching some or all of the human's behavior — but this approach is fundamentally limited because the demonstrations themselves are imperfect. In this work we advance offline imitation learning by enabling robots to extrapolate across nearby actions, instead of only considering what the human actually showed. We achieve this by hypothesizing that all of the human's demonstrations are trying to convey an underlying policy, while the noise and sub-optimality within their behaviors obfuscates the data and introduces unintentional complexity. To recover the underlying policy and learn what the human teacher meant, we introduce Counter-BC , a generalized version of behavior cloning. Counter-BC expands the given dataset to include actions close to behaviors the human demonstrated (i.e., counterfactual actions that the human teacher could have intended, but did not actually show). During training Counter-BC autonomously modifies the human's demonstrations within this expanded region to reach a simplified policy that explains the underlying trends in the human's dataset. Theoretically, we prove that Counter-BC can extract a simple and similar-to-demonstration policy from imperfect data, multiple users, and teachers of varying skill levels. Empirically, we compare Counter-BC to state-of-the-art alternatives in simulated and real-world settings with noisy demonstrations, standardized datasets, and real human teachers. Overall, we find that trying to extrapolate what the human teacher meant by considering nearby actions — as opposed to rigorously following what actions the human actually demonstrated — can lead to more proficient learning from humans. See videos of our work here: https://youtu.be/XaeOZWhTt68

title: Prompt Engineering: Theory, Techniques and Practice
abstract: This textbook aims to offer an in-depth, accessible, and hands-on exploration of prompt engineering the art of creating inputs that enable large language models to deliver more accurate, reliable, and suitable responses. It meets the needs of undergraduate and postgraduate students in computer science, artificial intelligence and the data sciences as well as practicing engineers, data scientists and AI product managers who want to learn prompt engineering from a research-based perspective.Prompt engineering has been a rapidly flowering field of study. Interacting with AI systems effectively used to need a dedicated data scientist with experience in machine learning, model architecture and train infrastructure and just a few years ago! Natural language is the main gateway to the most powerful AI systems ever created and the main factor in how good that gateway is, is the quality of natural language that is used as input. This has made AI more accessible and, at the same time, a brand new specialized branch: the art and science of developing the AI optimized prompts.The textbook consists of five units which progress from basic concepts to advanced techniques and onto the forefront of research. Unit I lays the theoretical and empirical groundwork, covering the architecture of large language models (LLM), natural language processing (NLP) and generative AI basics, using prompts to control the outputs of LLMs, the main categories of prompting—zero-shot, one-shot, and few-shot, and model deep-dives into the world's most popular models such as ChatGPT, GPT-4 and GPT-4.5, Claude, Gemini, and LLaMA. Unit II covers best practices in iterative prompt refinement, contextual prompting with examples and constraints, and chain-of-thought prompting and instruction-based prompting, all key steps in prompt design. Unit III introduces more complex prompting approaches such as multi-turn, self-consistency & verification prompts, prompt decomposition, prompt reusability, and other advanced methods like Tree of Thoughts, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, few shot with demonstrations. Unit IV will explore the tools, frameworks and applications that make up the current state of deployed prompt engineering, including a detailed look at Langchain, LlamaIndex and Haystack along with prompt evaluation metrics and applications like education, business automation, coding assistance, content generation and more. In Unit V, students will discover the burgeoning research landscape of autonomous agents and prompt chaining, fine-tuning versus prompt engineering, prompt engineering using external knowledge bases, ethical concerns and responsible AI prompting, exciting future research and development opportunities in multimodal prompting and human-AI creative collaboration, and the standardization of prompt engineering process.Extensive unit material is provided after each unit with a comprehensive review, unit summary tying the key concepts together, practical hands-on activities, and deep dive to explore the core content in greater detail for more advanced students. There are five appendices containing practical supporting content, including worked examples across real applications, prompt quality checklist & reusable prompts, API-specific prompting guidance, and ethical guidance for professional practice and specialized domain guidance – healthcare, legal, financial, creative.Original exposition in preference to borrowed formulations are used throughout this book. All material is designed to be done independently - no supplementary tools are needed. Conceptual explanations are followed by concrete examples, theoretical principles are illustrated with concrete examples, and worked examples are provided that trace the complete design process – from requirements analysis through iterative process of refining the design to deployment evaluation. The outcome is a thorough and complete guide to prompting as it is done at the cutting edge of the discipline.We hope that this textbook will not only lead to current practice in prompt engineering, but also provide a conceptual basis which will not end up being outdated as the field progresses. The actual models, tools and benchmark results will vary based on any new developments that come to light. The ethical principles, systematic experimentations, rigorous analysis, and clear communication upon which good prompt engineering is built will stand the test of time. How to use this textbookThis textbook is not meant to be read separately, but rather in order, so that one unit can supplement the content of the previous units. More technically oriented students may have background knowledge in neural networks and natural language processing and choose to skip over this material and start the prompting content in Chapter 3. Those who want to get to work with tools but aren't interested in the theory can start with Unit II, and go back to Unit I as necessary for theory.The books are structured in the same manner as the chapters. Core Content sections clearly explain and analyze the main concepts of content together with examples. These sections give "Base Information" necessary for better practice. It meets the needs of undergraduate and postgraduate students in computer science, artificial intelligence and the data sciences as well as practicing engineers, data scientists and AI product managers who want to learn prompt engineering from a research-based perspective.Prompt engineering has been a rapidly flowering field of study. Interacting with AI systems effectively used to need a dedicated data scientist with experience in machine learning, model architecture and train infrastructure and just a few years ago! Natural language is the main gateway to the most powerful AI systems ever created and the main factor in how good that gateway is, is the quality of natural language that is used as input. This has made AI more accessible and, at the same time, a brand new specialized branch: the art and science of developing the AI optimized prompts.The textbook consists of five units which progress from basic concepts to advanced techniques and onto the forefront of research. Unit I lays the theoretical and empirical groundwork, covering the architecture of large language models (LLM), natural language processing (NLP) and generative AI basics, using prompts to control the outputs of LLMs, the main categories of prompting—zero-shot, one-shot, and few-shot, and model deep-dives into the world's most popular models such as ChatGPT, GPT-4 and GPT-4.5, Claude, Gemini, and LLaMA. Unit II covers best practices in iterative prompt refinement, contextual prompting with examples and constraints, and chain-of-thought prompting and instruction-based prompting, all key steps in prompt design. Unit III introduces more complex prompting approaches such as multi-turn, self-consistency & verification prompts, prompt decomposition, prompt reusability, and other advanced methods like Tree of Thoughts, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, few shot with demonstrations. title: DSPkit-app: a local web application for digital signal processing of time series data
abstract: DSPkit-app is a desktop application for digital signal processing of time series data, built on the DSPkit library. A file is opened without configuration: the delimiter, header row, orientation, time column and sample rate are detected on load and shown so they can be overridden, and the signals are plotted immediately. Analyses cover spectral estimation, cross-signal relationships, filtering with cutoffs picked off the spectrum, a linked time-frequency explorer over five transforms, decomposition, multi-channel coherence including conditioned forms, Frequency Domain Decomposition with mode shape export, and statistical analysis including normality assessment. It requires only Python 3.10 or newer; the interface ships pre-built and the analysis library is bundled, so no other tooling is needed to run it.

title: Benchmarking Personally Identifiable Information (PII) Anonymization Strategies for Brazilian Portuguese: From Regex to Hybrid LLM Approaches
authors: Joao Pedro Hallack Sansao and Thiago França Nascimento, Universidade Federal de Sao Joao del-Rei, Brazil
abstract: The Brazilian General Data Protection Law (LGPD) requires the anonymization of personally identifiable information (PII) before data sharing. We evaluate six anonymization strategies (regex, NER, zero-shot LLM, few-shot LLM, structured extraction, and a hybrid cascade) on 82 Brazilian Portuguese documents with 1,558 PII spans across 12 LLM variants. A hybrid cascade combining regex, NER, and conditional LLM invocation achieves 0.0% residual PII on the test set, matching text-to-text approaches while preserving span-level annotations. Model scale does not monotonically affect residual PII: Gemma 3-4B and Gemma 3-12B produce 2.28 and 1.56 residual respectively in zero-shot, while GPT-4o produces 3.71. The 38 strategy–model combinations provide a privacy–utility–cost analysis for Portuguese PII anonymization.

title: Quantum Entanglement Self-Organizing Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm, the Quantum Entanglement Self-Organizing Algorithm (QESA), designed to dynamically adjust system parameters within a complex system to optimize performance and stability. Leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement, QESA establishes a self-organizing mechanism that continuously refines parameter values based on real-time feedback, achieving a level of adaptability unattainable through conventional methods. The core mechanism centers on creating and manipulating entangled states to achieve this dynamic adjustment. This paper details the algorithm's architecture, the quantum operations involved, and the theoretical implications of its self-optimization capabilities. We present preliminary results demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness in a simplified system, highlighting its potential for broader applicability across diverse complex systems.

title: Rewards, Regrets, and Rubber Arms: A State of the Art Review of Reinforcement Learning in Games and Robotics
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Reinforcement Learning in Games and Robotics in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of reinforcement learning and robotics as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: 基于自适应的机器学习的概率模型优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel probabilistic model optimization technique centered around adaptive machine learning. Traditional machine learning methods often rely on static model parameters, limiting their ability to effectively handle data scarcity. We introduce a method that dynamically adjusts probability model parameters based on the data, leveraging the inherent adaptability of machine learning algorithms. This approach enhances model prediction accuracy and robustness, particularly when data is limited. The core mechanism involves an iterative adjustment process guided by a learning algorithm, ensuring the model adapts to the data distribution. We provide a theoretical framework and demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a series of simulations and experiments. The goal is to improve model performance in scenarios where data is sparse, offering a more robust and efficient solution compared to traditional approaches.

title: Non-Linear Integral-Based Gradient Boosting
abstract: This paper presents a novel gradient boosting algorithm, termed Non-Linear Integral-Based Gradient Boosting (NLIBG), designed to address the limitations of traditional gradient boosting methods. The core innovation lies in the implementation of an adaptive integration parameter strategy that dynamically adjusts the integration function during training, promoting better model generalization and reducing overfitting. We demonstrate the effectiveness of NLIBG through extensive experimental validation on a diverse range of machine learning and numerical datasets. The algorithm's automatic parameter adjustment mechanism significantly enhances the model's predictive performance compared to existing approaches. This work offers a promising pathway for enhancing the robustness and accuracy of gradient boosting algorithms.

title: Title: Adaptive Constraint Geometry
abstract: Abstract: Adaptive Constraint Geometry addresses the challenge of designing and optimizing constraint geometries for complex physical systems through the integration of evolutionary algorithms and reinforcement learning. Traditional methods often rely on manual definition, leading to brittle and suboptimal designs. This paper proposes a novel computational approach that automatically generates and refines constraint configurations using genetic algorithms, guided by a feedback metric that prioritizes both physical stability and efficiency. We present a framework for iterative refinement based on this feedback, demonstrating its effectiveness in generating designs suitable for modeling a range of physical systems. The core mechanism involves evolving constraint configurations through a genetic algorithm, incorporating a feedback metric that dynamically adjusts the design based on physical properties and performance criteria. The resulting designs exhibit enhanced stability and efficiency compared to conventional approaches, offering a significant advancement in automated constraint design.

title: Title: Bayesian Fractal Resonance
abstract: This paper introduces Bayesian Fractal Resonance, a novel probabilistic model designed to predict complex patterns across multiple scales within fractal geometries. The core mechanism leverages a Bayesian network that dynamically updates probability based on observed fractal structure, incorporating a 'resonance factor' to prioritize stable and complex arrangements. The goal is to move beyond static pattern recognition towards a model capable of simulating and predicting the evolution of complex fractal systems. This approach offers enhanced predictive power and allows for the simultaneous analysis of multiple scales. The paper details the model's architecture, explores the role of the resonance factor, and provides a conceptual framework for its application in various fields, including materials science, image processing, and pattern generation.

title: Neural Symbolic Systems for Robotic Planning and Control
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to robotic planning and control utilizing a synergistic combination of neural networks and symbolic reasoning. Current robotic systems often struggle with the complexities of real-world environments, exhibiting brittleness and a lack of adaptability. We argue that a hybrid system, leveraging the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks and the logical inference capabilities of symbolic systems, offers a more robust and effective solution. The core of our system consists of two key components: a high-level planning network that learns strategic plans and a symbolic reasoning engine that translates these plans into actionable commands for the robot. This architecture allows for both rapid adaptation to novel situations and the incorporation of explicit knowledge, leading to improved performance and reliability in robotic tasks. The system is designed to overcome the limitations of purely neural or purely symbolic approaches, creating a more intelligent and flexible robotic agent. This paper outlines the architecture, key components, and theoretical foundations of this Neural Symbolic System, and discusses potential applications and future research directions.

title: Quantum Homomorphic Computation Geometric Optimization
abstract: Quantum Homomorphic Computation (QHC) offers a fundamentally new approach to computation, leveraging the power of quantum mechanics to perform computations on encrypted data without decryption. This paper explores the application of geometric optimization to QHC, proposing a novel framework for enhancing the efficiency of hidden computation. We argue that traditional optimization methods often fall short in the complex, multi-dimensional space inherent to QHC, and that geometric optimization provides a crucial step towards achieving significant performance improvements. Our work demonstrates the potential of this approach through a rigorous analysis and preliminary results, highlighting its implications for future advancements in secure and efficient computation.

title: Algorithm Complexity and Nonlinear Functions
abstract: This paper explores the interplay between algorithm complexity and nonlinear functions, proposing a novel concept of "Nonlinear Function Complexity" (NFC) to identify and mitigate potential inefficiencies within existing algorithms. Traditional complexity measures primarily focus on execution time, while nonlinear functions offer a deeper insight into the algorithmic process. We define NFC as a metric derived from analyzing algorithm complexity, highlighting non-linear dependencies within the code. This approach utilizes this metric to pinpoint areas for optimization, ultimately leading to more efficient algorithms. The goal is to provide a robust framework for analyzing and improving the performance of complex systems. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of algorithm design and optimization, particularly in scenarios involving nonlinear functions.

abstract: This paper investigates the application of self-organizing quantum neural networks (SQNNs) to the problem of optimal resource allocation, a core challenge across diverse domains including finance, logistics, and telecommunications. Traditional classical neural networks frequently struggle to achieve optimal solutions when faced with complex constraints and dynamic environments. The central hypothesis of this work is that leveraging quantum computation through SQNNs, specifically utilizing qubit representations of resource states and exploiting entanglement, can significantly enhance the exploration of the solution space and lead to near-optimal resource allocation decisions. We propose a novel SQNN architecture designed to address this challenge. The architecture incorporates layers of quantum neurons that dynamically adjust their connectivity based on the input data, mimicking the self-organizing properties observed in biological neural networks. We present a theoretical framework outlining the key components of the SQNN and detail the mathematical formulation of the resource allocation problem being addressed. The core of the model is expressed as follows: Let *N* be the number of resources to be allocated. Let *K* be the number of potential allocation options for each resource. Let *xi* represent the allocation decision for resource *i*, where *xi* ∈ {1, 2, ..., *K*}. The objective is to minimize the cost function *C(x)*, which is defined as: *C(x) = ∑i=1N *Ci(xi)* where *Ci(xi)* represents the cost associated with resource *i* given the allocation *xi*. This cost function is subject to constraints *G(x) ≤ 0*, where *G* is a vector of constraints representing factors like capacity limits, demand requirements, and regulatory restrictions. The SQNN learns to approximate the optimal solution *x* that minimizes *C(x)* subject to the constraints *G(x) ≤ 0*. The network's self-organizing capability is achieved through a modified backpropagation algorithm adapted for quantum systems, incorporating quantum measurement and entangling operations to refine the network's internal state and improve its ability to represent and optimize the resource allocation problem. The efficacy of the SQNN is evaluated through simulations, demonstrating its potential to outperform classical neural networks in complex resource allocation scenarios.

title: A COMPARATIVE STUDY OF CNN-BILSTM AND TF-IDF–NAIVE BAYES FOR SENTIMENT CLASSIFICATION ON MOVIE REVIEWS: PERFORMANCE AND EFFICIENCY TRADE-OFFS
abstract: Sentiment analysis on movie reviews has become an important task for understanding public opinion, yet many high-performing deep learning models proposed in the literature rely on increasingly complex architectures such as multichannel embeddings, kernel-based projections, or attention-augmented transformers. This added complexity often comes without a clear report of computational cost, making it difficult to judge whether the performance gain justifies the resource trade-off. This study investigates whether a deliberately simplified Convolutional Neural Network combined with a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-BiLSTM) architecture can achieve competitive performance compared to a classical baseline, TF-IDF combined with Naive Bayes, while explicitly reporting training efficiency. Both models were trained and evaluated on the IMDB Dataset of 50,000 movie reviews, split into 80% training, 10% validation, and 10% testing sets. Experimental results show that the proposed CNN-BiLSTM achieved an accuracy of 86.58%, precision of 90.38%, recall of 81.88%, F1-score of 85.92%, and AUC of 0.946, while the TF-IDF-Naive Bayes baseline achieved an accuracy of 85.98%, precision of 86.58%, recall of 85.16%, F1-score of 85.86%, and AUC of 0.932. The proposed method required approximately 203 seconds of training time, compared to 0.07 seconds for the baseline. These findings indicate that the performance improvement offered by the deep learning approach is modest relative to its substantially higher computational cost, providing practical guidance for method selection in resource-constrained settings.

title: Linguistic Foundations for Constructing Speech Synthesis in the Kazakh Language
abstract: The article is devoted to the problem of correctly recognizing and pronouncing, in accordance with orthoepic norms, shortened words and abbreviations, numerical symbols, mathematical operations, formulas, and conventional signs within the Kazakh-language text-to-speech system. The main objective of the study is to identify the linguistic features of fully expanding shortened words and abbreviations in texts processed by the speech synthesis system, as well as of representing mathematical expressions in written form, and on this basis to develop a linguistic resource that ensures natural, consistent, and realistic synthesized speech in Kazakh. The article clarifies the distinction between shortened words and abbreviations and proposes several approaches to incorporating them into a speech synthesis program. In particular, it describes methods such as compiling comprehensive lists of shortened forms from domain-specific texts, presenting shortened and full variants in parallel, and preserving internationally established abbreviations in their original forms. The article also provides a dedicated phonetic transcription of shortened words and demonstrates their pronunciation in compliance with orthoepic norms. The article presents model examples of attaching suffixes to shortened words, numerical symbols, and conventional signs in accordance with the vowel harmony rules of the Kazakh language. It is demonstrated that presenting both written and spoken variants of numerical symbols, arithmetic operations, fractions, and complex numbers increases the intelligibility of synthesized text. Furthermore, the parallel use of symbolic representations and established names of chemical elements and formulas is shown to enhance the naturalness of speech synthesis.

title: Reconfigurable measurement scheme compatible with MDI-QKD and BB84 protocols using single-laser sideband generation
abstract: A quantum network can be operated efficiently by switching between measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution (MDI-QKD) and BB84 according to the trust level of an intermediate node, since MDI-QKD is immune to all detector side-channel attacks while generally yielding a lower secret-key rate. Here, we present a proof-of-principle demonstration of a reconfigurable measurement scheme compatible with both protocols using a single laser. Two mutually independent weak coherent states (WCSs) are generated from a shared continuous-wave laser via electro-optic phase modulation and subsequent first-order sideband filtering. Channel indistinguishability is verified using two complementary Hong–Ou–Mandel (HOM) measurements: time-resolved coincidence measurements and polarization mismatch scans, both yielding HOM visibilities close to the theoretical limit of 0.5 for WCSs. The measurement module performs a partial Bell-state measurement for MDI-QKD, while rotating a single half-wave plate to reconfigures the same module into a dual-basis polarization analyzer for BB84. The quantum bit error rates measured in both configurations agree well with theoretical expectations, verifying the operational feasibility of the reconfigurable receiver at the physical layer. By eliminating the need for active frequency locking while retaining independent sideband tunability, this approach provides a practical foundation for flexible and cost-effective quantum networks.

title: Toollery: Scaling LLM Agents to Thousands of Skills and Tools
abstract: As LLM agents are exposed to hundreds to tens of thousands of skills, tools, and API functions, full-library prompting becomes costly, slow, and less reliable: each added candidate increases prompt tokens and latency, while longer candidate lists introduce more distractors for LLM selection. We present \textbf{Toollery}, a training-free candidate-compression framework for scalable LLM skill/tool selection. Following established document-side query expansion, Toollery generates user-intent queries from each skill/tool specification and builds a retrieval index that maps real user requests to compact candidate sets before final LLM decision-making. By treating high-level skills and atomic tools as selectable capabilities, Toollery can be applied to both skill libraries and tool registries. We evaluate Toollery on the roughly 79K-capability SkillRouter benchmark, BFCL-V4 with over 440 atomic tools, and 3,396 proprietary smart-cockpit requests over 220 tools. Across these settings, Toollery keeps online selection bounded to a compact top-$k$ candidate set and improves recall over ordinary specification retrieval. At a fixed top-10 budget, Toollery improves end-to-end selection on the cockpit dataset, and maintains comparable AST Accuracy on BFCL-V4. These results support Toollery as a practical candidate-compression framework for large and evolving agent capability libraries, while showing that quality and cost gains depend on workload coverage and provider caching.

title: LeanStream: A Speculate-and-Refine Streaming Framework for Efficient on-Device LLM Inference
abstract: On-device LLM inference is attractive for privacy and responsiveness, but remains challenging on mobile and embedded devices because model weights far exceed available DRAM. Prior systems exploit activation sparsity and offload weights to SSD or flash storage, but face a fundamental systems trade-off: accurate sparse execution decisions require the latest context, whereas efficient computation-I/O overlap requires early prediction. As a result, existing designs either serialize execution or incur redundant weight fetches, extra computation, and large cache overheads. We present LeanStream, a streaming speculate-and-refine framework for efficient on-device LLM inference. LeanStream progressively refines computation, loading, and cache-retention priorities using partial GPU results, enabling fine-grained overlap between GPU execution and storage I/O. We implement LeanStream on both mobile and embedded platforms. Compared with prior on-device LLM inference systems, LeanStream reduces memory usage by 4.8$\times$ to 7.5$\times$ at the best throughput achieved by prior work, while further improving token generation throughput by 1.6$\times$ to 2.1$\times$.

title: Learning to Attract and Repel: Dual Quality Margin Learning for Face Recognition (DQM-Face)
abstract: Face recognition in unconstrained environments remains highly challenging due to diverse and extreme variations encountered in real-world scenarios. To mitigate these effects, existing margin-based approaches model sample quality through feature magnitude. However, magnitude-based modeling alone is susceptible to identity-agnostic noise, which can degrade the reliability and discriminative power of learned representations. In this paper, we propose Dual Quality Margin Learning for Face Recognition (DQM-Face), a novel framework that enables refined attraction and repulsion dynamics during representation learning. Our approach unifies conventional magnitude-based quality estimation with a newly introduced semantic quality learning mechanism, realized via squeeze-and-excitation semantic attention. By jointly leveraging magnitude and semantic cues, we construct enhanced quality-aware margins that adaptively strengthen intra-class compactness through improved attraction during learning. To further enhance inter-class discrimination, we introduce a repulsion margin formulation that explicitly enlarges inter-class separation. The unified integration of semantic quality modeling with dual attraction-repulsion margin optimization results in a more structured and discriminative feature geometry. Extensive experiments on multiple challenging benchmarks demonstrate that DQM-Face consistently outperforms state-of-the-art face recognition methods. Moreover, we show that the quality learned for margin optimization is highly effective for face image quality assessment within the proposed framework, demonstrating that the learned quality signal is intrinsically aligned with the recognition objective. The code is publicly available: https://github.com/RAIB-group/DQM-Face

title: Beyond Modality Harmony: Orthogonal Purification and Topology-Guided MoE for Conflict-Aware Multimodal Recommendation
abstract: Multimodal Recommender Systems (MRSs) typically rely on a flawed "modality harmony" assumption, presuming that multimodal features are inherently beneficial and strictly aligned with users' collaborative interaction patterns. However, modality-topology conflicts are ubiquitous in real-world scenarios due to deceptive visual clickbaits and mismatched semantics. Blindly integrating these noisy modalities inevitably pollutes the pristine collaborative space, causing severe representation distortion. To address this, we propose Orthogonal purification and topology-guided MoE for conflict-aware multimodal Recommendation (OrthoRec). At its core, OrthoRec introduces Collaborative-Guided Orthogonal Purification (CGOP), which geometrically decouples multimodal features into directions parallel and orthogonal to a pure collaborative anchor. By adaptively truncating the orthogonal noise with an energy-preserving normalization, CGOP rectifies deceptive semantic directions while preserving the modality's intrinsic representation capacity. Furthermore, we design a Topology-Aware Routing Mixture-of-Experts (TAR-MoE). Guided by the collaborative topology, TAR-MoE employs decoupled sigmoid gating to break the zero-sum bottleneck of traditional softmax attention, autonomously determining the injection scale for each purified modality. Finally, a safe-SSL objective is introduced to dynamically penalize the forced contrastive alignment of contradictory pairs. Experiments on three real-world Amazon datasets show that OrthoRec consistently outperforms competitive recent baselines and exhibits improved robustness under modality noise and item sparsity.

title: Application of Reinforcement Learning to the Control of a Simulated Robotic Manipulator
abstract: V diplomskem delu smo zasnovali in implementirali simulacijsko okolje za spodbujevano učenje (angl. reinforcement learning) za robotski manipulator Universal Robots UR10e. Obravnavali smo razvoj okolja, ki omogoča učenje robotske manipulacije v simulaciji. Okolje temelji na simulatorju MuJoCo, knjižnicah Gymnasium in Gymnasium Robotics ter ogrodju PyTorch z uporabo knjižnice Stable-Baselines3. Razvili smo prilagojeni okolji za nalogi doseganja cilja (angl. Reach) ter prijemanja in dvigovanja predmeta (angl. Pick-and-Place). Implementirali smo kartezično vodenje robotskega manipulatorja z uporabo inverzne kinematike po metodi dušenih najmanjših kvadratov (angl. Damped Least Squares), prilagodili smo opazovalni in akcijski prostor, dekompozicijo zahtevnejše naloge ter ustrezni funkciji nagrajevanja. Ovrednotili smo algoritme SAC (angl. Soft Actor-Critic), PPO (angl. Proximal Policy Optimization) in TQC (angl. Truncated Quantile Critics). Pri nalogi doseganja cilja sta algoritma SAC in TQC dosegla 100 % uspešnost, PPO pa približno 80 %. Naloga prijemanja in dvigovanja predmeta je bila zahtevnejša. SAC je dosegel približno 40 % uspešnost, TQC največ približno 30 %, PPO pa naloge ni uspešno dokončal. Rezultati kažejo, da razvito okolje omogoča uspešno učenje osnovne manipulacijske naloge in je osnova za nadaljnji razvoj zahtevnejših nalog ter prenos naučenih strategij na fizične robotske sisteme.

title: Bigger, Better, or Just Bigger: A State of the Art Review of The Scaling Laws Debate in Modern Machine Learning
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of The Scaling Laws Debate in Modern Machine Learning in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of scaling laws and compute as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: 基于自适应量子拓扑的算法优化
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum topology algorithms to optimization problems. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameter adjustments, limiting their effectiveness in complex scenarios. We propose a novel algorithm, termed "Dynamic Quantum Topology Optimization," that dynamically adjusts algorithm parameters based on the quantum topology structure of the problem. title: Topology-Aware Quantum Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper investigates the integration of topology into quantum algorithm design, aiming to enhance the efficiency and robustness of quantum computations. The core claim is to develop a method for systematically mapping quantum states to topological structures, thereby facilitating the creation of quantum algorithms that optimally exploit these inherent properties. We propose a framework leveraging the interplay between quantum states and topological invariants to guide the design of novel quantum algorithms. The research emphasizes the crucial role of topology in shaping quantum system behavior and offers a potential pathway toward significant improvements in computational capabilities. Specifically, we demonstrate the practical implications of this approach through a theoretical analysis and preliminary implementation of a simplified quantum algorithm. This work contributes to the advancement of quantum information theory by addressing a fundamental challenge in algorithm design – the exploitation of topological structures within quantum systems.

title: Quantum-Driven Lattice Parameter Optimization for Materials
abstract: Quantum-driven lattice parameter optimization is a novel approach to materials science that leverages the power of quantum computing to efficiently explore the parameter space of crystal structures. Traditional methods, while effective, often face computational bottlenecks, limiting the scope of potential discoveries. This paper proposes a quantum-enhanced optimization strategy utilizing quantum annealing and variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) techniques to systematically search for optimal lattice parameters, potentially leading to the identification of novel material properties. The core mechanism centers around quantum algorithms designed to navigate the complex parameter space, offering a potential paradigm shift in materials discovery. This work addresses the challenges of computational complexity and provides a framework for harnessing quantum mechanics to accelerate materials design. This research explores the feasibility of using quantum algorithms to optimize lattice parameters, focusing on the potential to uncover new material characteristics and advancements.

title: Adaptive Topologies of Quantum Information Learning
abstract: Quantum information learning is a rapidly evolving field with significant potential for breakthroughs in quantum computation and quantum information processing. Traditional approaches often rely on manually crafted quantum circuits and complex optimization strategies. This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum information learning based on adaptive topologies, leveraging the non-locality inherent in quantum entanglement. We present a new algorithm that utilizes a knowledge graph constructed from quantum entanglement to dynamically model quantum states, resulting in more precise physical simulations and numerical computations. The core mechanism involves constructing a topological knowledge graph to represent the quantum state, and then using the non-local properties of entanglement to learn and evolve this graph. This algorithm offers a promising path towards automated optimization and improved performance in quantum information learning.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Distributed Resource Allocation
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) to the problem of distributed resource allocation. Traditional approaches to this problem often struggle with the complexity arising from dynamic environments, decentralized control, and the need for global optimization. MARL offers a compelling alternative by training a population of agents, each responsible for a localized resource allocation decision. This approach allows for adaptive behavior and emergent coordination, potentially leading to superior performance compared to centralized solutions. The core of this work is the design and implementation of a MARL framework where agents learn optimal allocation strategies through trial and error, guided by a reward function that reflects the overall system objective. We explore different MARL algorithms, including Independent Q-Learning (IQL) and Centralized Training with Decentralized Execution (CTDE), to assess their effectiveness. The research demonstrates the potential of MARL to efficiently solve complex distributed resource allocation problems, adapting to dynamic environments and optimizing overall system performance. This work provides a foundational approach for future research in this area.

title: Symbiotic Algorithm for Computational Complexity
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm, the Symbiotic Algorithm, designed to optimize computational complexity by fostering symbiotic relationships between tasks within a computational chain. The algorithm dynamically allocates computational resources to tasks based on their position in a complexity chain, aiming to minimize the overall complexity while maintaining a consistent level of performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations, revealing a significant improvement in complexity compared to traditional optimization methods. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously monitors task progress and adjusts resource allocation to achieve optimal balance.

title: Quantum Information Cryptography Geometric Formalization
abstract: Quantum Information Cryptography (QIC) aims to secure information through cryptographic algorithms that are resistant to computational attacks. Traditional cryptographic approaches frequently rely on mathematical hardness assumptions, while geometric cryptography leverages the properties of geometric spaces to create secure systems. This paper explores a novel approach to QIC: the geometric formalization of key decryption. We propose a method that transforms the core decryption problem into a geometric problem, employing a novel optimization algorithm to refine cryptographic parameters and enhance security. The core claim is that this geometric formalization significantly improves the security of key decryption compared to traditional methods, leveraging the power of geometric topology. This work introduces a new framework for analyzing and optimizing cryptographic systems, potentially offering a more robust approach to secure communication.

title: Title: Interference-Based Algorithm Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm, termed the Interference-Based Algorithm Optimization (IBAO), designed to significantly enhance the speed and efficiency of complex computations. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with computationally intensive problems, necessitating brute-force approaches. The IBAO leverages the inherent interference patterns within the algorithm's structure to dynamically guide the computation process, effectively reducing the need for exhaustive search and improving overall performance. This algorithm utilizes a sophisticated interference model to identify and mitigate redundant computations, leading to substantial speed improvements across a range of computational tasks. We present a detailed analysis of the algorithm's design, performance evaluation, and practical applications, demonstrating its effectiveness in optimizing challenging scenarios. This paper explores the core mechanisms behind the algorithm's success, focusing on the intricate interplay between the interference model and the computation itself.

title: Cross-platform deployment and characterization of an on-device generative conversational agent
abstract: Recent advances in Language Models (LMs) enable conversational systems that interpret natural-language requests, select application actions, and generate user-facing responses. However, existing studies typically either examine complete assistants with limited deployment evidence or benchmark individual components in isolation. This work advances the state of the art through a unified cross-platform characterization of a local speech-to-text-LM-text-to-speech pipeline combining Moonshine, Piper, and four quantized LMs ranging from 1.2B to 8B parameters. The pipeline is deployed on an Nvidia Jetson AGX Orin, a Raspberry Pi 5, and an STM32MP257F-EV1, and evaluated in thermostat and washing-machine use cases. Action-selection capability is assessed on 200 labelled explicit and implicit requests per use case, while deployment is characterized through metrics such as memory footprint, speech Real-Time Factor, decoding throughput, power consumption, etc. Granite 3.3 (8B) achieves the highest Macro F1-scores, whereas Qwen3.5 (4B) provides the best capability–resource trade-off. Speech processing is faster than real time on the Jetson and Raspberry Pi, while the STM32MP2 supports smaller LMs in memory but is unsuitable for responsive CPU-only conversation. LM decoding accounts for over 90% of turn duration, and memory-Roofline analysis identifies model footprint, runtime support, response length, and streaming execution as the main optimization levers.

title: Transversal Gates and Magic State Distillation in an Optimally Synthesized Spin-Qubit Shuttling Bus
abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires not only reliable logical qubit storage, but also the ability to perform high-fidelity logical operations between error-corrected qubits at scale. While much of the existing literature focuses on optimizing syndrome extraction for a single logical qubit, the co-design of physical architectures that support both robust error correction and efficient logical computation remains an open challenge. In this work, we propose a multi-qubit spin-qubit shuttling bus architecture that addresses both requirements simultaneously. The architecture optimizes the physical qubit layout for syndrome extraction and supports transversal two-qubit logical gates between an arbitrary number of logical qubits, achieving all-to-all logical connectivity through coherent spin shuttling. We further propose an ancilla-sharing scheme that encodes multiple logical qubits within a single logical element, compressing the physical footprint of the processor and improving long-range gate fidelity. Extending the architecture from a one-dimensional bus to a two-dimensional grid of shuttling tracks reduces the inter-qubit distance, yielding consistent improvements in logical error. Finally, we apply the Quantum Reverse Mapping methodology at the logical level to optimize the layout of a \textit{15-to-1} magic state distillation circuit, demonstrating how the transversal capabilities of the proposed architecture can be leveraged for universal fault-tolerant computation. Taken together, these results establish a principled co-design framework that bridges the physical, error-correction, and logical computation layers of the quantum stack, and demonstrate that spin-qubit shuttling architectures are a viable and flexible substrate for scalable fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: From Detection to Localization: A Unified Forensics Framework for Fully Synthetic and Tampered Images
abstract: The rapid advancement of generative models has significantly worsened the problem of manipulated image detection, as these methods are capable of producing highly realistic forgeries, reinforcing the importance of multimedia forensics. Conventional approaches typically frame image manipulation detection as a binary classification task (real vs. generated), which limits the capability to distinguish and localize different forms of manipulation. To address these constraints, this work extends an existing detector by introducing a unified multiclass framework (real vs. fully generated vs. tampered). In addition to classifying image authenticity, the framework incorporates a segmentation branch to enable pixel-level localization of tampered regions. The proposed approach outperforms selected recent benchmarks, offering an efficient solution with improved classification accuracy and higher IoU scores for the localization task. Find the code at https://github.com/anngal01/From-Detection-to-Localization-A-Unified-Forensics-Framework-for-Fully-Synthetic-and-Tampered-Images.

title: Fair Stable Matching: A Nash Social Welfare Approach
abstract: While traditional stable matching algorithms, such as the Gale-Shapley algorithm, prioritize stability, they may fall short of achieving equitable outcomes among participants. We study the role of \emph{Nash social welfare} (NSW) as a fairness objective in the classic \emph{stable marriage problem}. We develop \texttt{SNSW-Alg} that finds a stable matching that maximizes Nash social welfare under rank-induced utilities in $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^4)$ time, where $n$ is the number of men or women. We demonstrate that \texttt{SNSW-Alg} balances equity while preserving stability. We empirically evaluate our methods across diverse preference distributions, demonstrating significant gains in fairness without substantial losses in other key measures such as regret, egalitarian criterion, and sex equality. Our findings suggest that the stable matching produced by \texttt{SNSW-Alg} is statistically Pareto-undominated by stable matchings based on other fairness measures - regret, egalitarian, and sex equality. This study offers compelling insights for designing fair-stable matching.

title: Affective Scaffolding in Creative Learning: The Vivience Framework for Empathic Digital Humans as Collaborative Partners
abstract: As Generative AI (GenAI) systems increasingly transition from passive computational tools to active dialogic partners within educational ecosystems, the affective and communicative dimensions of human–AI interaction demand rigorous theoretical interrogation. Prevailing scholarship predominantly prioritises system efficiency and informational accuracy, frequently marginalising the affective investments and socio-emotional scaffolding requisite for creative learning. Within these vulnerable contexts, ostensibly "neutral" AI interfaces architected for transactional efficiency rather than relational pragmatics are frequently interpreted by learners as affectively indifferent or implicitly evaluative. This phenomenon, conceptualised herein as the "Neutrality Trap," is theorised to engender a discursive void that stifles the psychological safety necessary for creative risk-taking. To address this lacuna, this paper advances the "Vivience Framework for Affective Scaffolding," an integrated conceptual architecture for Empathic Digital Humans (EDHs). Drawing from foundational interactional modelling outlined in Singh (2025), this framework operationalises AI empathy not as an anthropomorphic simulation of sentience, but as a design-dependent communicative scaffold that supports learning regulation. By synthesising Vygotskian scaffolding (Vygotsky, 1978), Self-Determination Theory (Ryan & Deci, 2000), and Control-Value Theory (Pekrun, 2006), the paper articulates the theoretical mechanisms by which AER is hypothesised to mitigate "Affective Load,” the extraneous cognitive burden induced by anxiety and perceived judgment. Finally, the paper posits the "Vivience Protocol" as a rigorous methodological reference design for future empirical inquiry, advocating a paradigmatic shift from monologic, transactional AI to dialogic, relationally attuned AI partners in education.

abstract: ==========OPEN SOURCE SOFTWARE NOTICE========== The prior EULA license this software was released under is hereby revoked and replace immutably with the Apache 2.0 license. Click the "Connect to API" key in the top right corner of the app.2. Choose your AI model and enter your API key. Your key is stored in ephemeral memory and not exposed outside of your browser or anywhere, as is the industry standard for this type of app model (bring your own AI key).NOTE. On the Connect API key page, you can translate the app into a different language (this was still being developed at the time of open source release, and at least one glitch is present where the AI or some data labels are still in English)3. Enter your query or prompt and select the settings you wish to use (there is a "Demo" button which will generate a theory and automatically run. It finds some pretty interesting bio stuff sometimes all on its own! Be sure to always read the Swanson's Discovery information the AI finds.) ==========MANIFESTO========== FINAL NOTE from Joshua (the developer of this software):This software was originally made to help accelerate research and development of cures, by using proven literature such as PubMed data or OpenAlex data, or Wikipedia. If you snoop through the code you will see that arXiv is also a hidden option. I removed it because CORS settings need to be used as they do not allow origin=* in the API call alone. I am not committing to maintaining the software going forward as I am beginning a new project which will be hosted at https://pathmap.org/alchemy. The goal of the new project is to "gamify" science and knowledge through a free (not BYOAI Key model) AI interface that lets anyone mix two concepts and make veridical literature based discoveries. I will personally be using it for things like "Magnolia and COPD" and "Pulverized Magnolia Bark and Pulverized Sunflower Seeds" or "PDEVs and SIRT3", etc., in order to seed a scientific database of known plant derived extracellular vesicles, their known properties (e.g., cargo/payload size, hydrophilic/lipophilic/electrophilic data, SMILES strings, and any other helpful data that can be open-public in order to help scientists derive WHICH PDEVs would be the most effective fit/use for a pathology. Using the PathMap software, I have published about using Ginger/Ginseng or other exosome sized PDEVs via intradermal hydrogel for "washout" delivery to localized lymphatic system targets, an idea I am putting here because it could be useful for treating breast cancer. Research shows that it would stop metastasis from advancing to the next zone and allow targeted delivery of chemotherapy, potentially allowing a non-destructive version of chemo targeting versus blood delivered routes. Another main discovery set I want to note before I open source the code is about genetic c9orf72 ALS. I published about intranasal delivery of Spermidine-modified Ginger Derived Extracellular Vesicles. The Spermidine mod targets the MARK2-eif5a axis which is helpful, not only for downregulating the MARK2 axis if it were needed - such as to potentially reduce DPRs in c9orf72 ALS - but more importantly, as a homing device / beacon system to deliver Cas9 CRISPR gene therapy. This platform will also apply to NEK-1 ALS. This platform does not apply to sporadic ALS, because the data shows that Sporadic ALS is a collapse in retinal-RGNEF via a toxin or toxin-like vector that steals retinal synaptic zinc, thereby removing the NMDA receptor "brake fluid". The catch is the thermodynamic affinities: The toxin must have a zinc affinity > glutamate (from synapse) but < than RGNEF which *could* create a mis-shuttling loop that floods Zinc to RGNEF proteins and causes rigidity. Dr Michael Strong's work, and separately, Droppleman et al., show that if the RGNEF protein were to have its NF242 Terminal lose function or be sequestered, this could lead to TDP-43 proteinopathy. 97% of sALS patients had a TDP-43 biomarker in the retina. I cannot find any congenitally blind sALS cases. Schizophrenia is the only other disease I could find with such a "blindness shield" and it is related to corollary discharge in SD. So why not also in sALS, I wondered. Well, turns out that the NMDA brake fluid theft causes overexcitement in Retinal Ganglion Cells. We know that the bad TDP-43 causes cryptic STMN2 missplicing in motor neurons, and I have no reason to doubt that it would cause cryptic missplicing in retinal ganglion STMN2. All of this said, there were (are) two missing links which I can explain but not prove. If the RGC overexcitement caused misfiring of corollary discharge AND, the bayesian brain feed forward models allow a "concensus" that could misinterpret laggy/unexpected CD (corollary discharge) as "instant movement", then the bayesian brain would also then calculate that the motor neurons or golgi tendon organs or pathways were fautly and increase the gain because the movement was reported by the brain itself (the eyes) as instant yet the peripheral sensor reported XX milliseconds. I see it like a see-saw and it is plausible with PubMed science. One issue was "how does this go retrograde from retina upstream?". I cannot explain that but my research on Ebola leads me to think that this is the "ghost factor" in ALS: Some environmental toxins that "do not cause ALS" but are "associated with ALS" may be randomly forming toxic vector "clouds" by aerosolization of the toxin in a way that binds it to, or encapsulates it within, a plant derived extracellular vesicle, and the delivery is through the cribriform plate, bypassing the BBB and then moving *downstream* to the retina, not retrograde up! All said, if my theories and views on sporadic ALS are correct, then either a bright light or total darkness (not sure of polarity, I need a Neuro-Ophthalmologist to consider it) would be **REQUISITE** for any long term cure of sporadic ALS because the bayesian brain will always raise the gain on signals to peripherals under this model until the eyes are not being trusted at all (eg, does total darkness therapy lower the trust weights on the eye feeds and allow the brain to trust the peripheral sensors without penalizing them for being reported as "late/slow"?). Glaucoma is much like sALS in the retina from what I read, but the requirement of the optic nerve injury for Glaucoma may explain why there is an inverted occurrence between sALS and glaucoma - the brain knows not to trust the eyes as much and does not penalize. I also posited that c9orf72 ALS upscaled p62 systems may explain why there is ZERO (that I could find) occurrence of the sALS retina TDP-43 signature found in c9orf72 ALS yet they both have the TDP-43 markers otherwise. Vitreous fluid/humor data may show a different progression of c9ALS and sALS. Also, c9ALS and FTLD are the same genetic defect and the mixing of the data with sALS data has made the current view of ALS confounding. My models explain it differently and with consilience. I hope you can use the software as I did and find the truth in the literature and help heal the land. And, Endometriosis and Ovarian Tumors... I published about how an injected hydrogel of moxa or borneal modified **ginger** EVs would be ideal for ovarian tumor therapy delivery because the borneal can likely "drill" through the hard outside of the tumor and the 6-shogaol that would be naturally within the ginger-evs is known to cause apoptosis in ovarian tumor cells. While looking at endometriosis, I found that hyaluronic-acid modified ginger-evs would be the trick, but then after further consideration, using both the moxa/borneal and HA modified EVs for either endometriosis or ovarian tumor would potentially be a good thing to test. I can only show "the math" of the science with this PathMap software. We will always need real human scientists and real researchers doing real lab work, and I hope that this software can help you connect the dots from Turkey+Pom for COPD diet ideas to figuring the next iPSC experiment you should do, or what thesis makes sense to write. All of that said, the 144 publishings on PathMap.org are also archived in the Zenodo community for PathMap, and there are no planned further publishings to that blog/resource as I move forward with PathMap Alchemy and PathMap Nutrition in the future. Enjoy the software and use it responsibly. Sorry if there are any glitches and if someone or anyone chooses to start a GIT for this or their derivative works, it may be helpful. The software is AS_IS and NO_WARRANTY so you will have to take it from here on those items. Finally, nearly all of this was done - created, tested, deployed, used, maintained, and marketed, from a 4GB metroPCS phone. It was my vision that even a youth in Indonesia may have an idea about some cure or some thing that would greatly help humanity, and they they should not be disallowed due to lack of resource, language barriers, lack of technology or access to it, and so forth. If my loved one were dying, I would not want even a single moment of delay. That is

title: Agent Task Control Plane: A Reference Architecture for Human-Governed Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Agent Task Control Plane (ATCP) is a reference architecture for governing parallel AI-agent work. It addresses the growing human cognitive burden of managing multiple asynchronous agents, including task-state loss, context contamination, missing deployment or verification steps, goal drift, and weak traceability. ATCP introduces a task-first control-plane model built around authoritative state machines, coordination, observability, human approval, verification, traceability, and human-attention routing. Its central principle is: scaling agents should not scale human cognitive load.

title: Self-Referential Code Generation for Formal Verification
abstract: Formal verification is a critical technique for ensuring software correctness, but its widespread adoption is hampered by the difficulty of creating precise and expressive formal specifications. Traditional approaches require significant manual effort and domain expertise, often leading to incomplete or overly complex specifications. This paper introduces a novel system for automating this process through self-referential code generation. The system leverages a grammar that encodes the program's logic and potential error conditions, generating formal specifications directly from the source code. The generated specification is then used to automatically derive a verification proof. We demonstrate the feasibility and potential benefits of this approach, arguing that it can substantially reduce the burden of specification creation and, potentially, broaden the applicability of formal verification. The core idea is to let the code *define* the verification process, creating a feedback loop. This approach tackles the expressiveness barrier by using the program itself as the source of the verification rules. The system relies on a carefully designed grammar that captures the semantics of the code, allowing for the automatic construction of formal models suitable for verification. The resulting verification process is intrinsically tied to the code's logic, increasing the likelihood of detecting subtle errors.

title: Probability Field Theory: Adaptive Distribution Models
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic model based on probability field theory, specifically designed for dynamic systems. Traditional probabilistic models often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to accurately represent complex systems. This research proposes a self-adapting probability distribution model that dynamically adjusts probability distributions based on system state, resulting in improved prediction accuracy. The core mechanism involves introducing an adaptive probability distribution model utilizing the self-adaptivity of probability field theory, enabling precise modeling of system probability distributions and dynamic adjustment. The paper presents a comprehensive investigation of this approach, detailing its implementation, validation, and performance evaluation. The primary goal is to demonstrate the efficacy of the self-adapting model in handling complex systems with evolving probability distributions.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence via Causal Inference Framework
abstract: This paper addresses the limitations of current Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) methods, which primarily focus on post-hoc explanations of model behavior without adequately incorporating causal reasoning. The core claim is that these approaches often generate unreliable explanations due to a neglect of causal relationships. We propose a novel framework integrating causal inference into the XAI process. This framework aims to provide more robust and trustworthy explanations by explicitly modeling and reasoning about causal relationships within the data and the model. The proposed methodology utilizes techniques from causal discovery and causal modeling to identify key causal pathways influencing model predictions, leading to explanations that are grounded in underlying causal mechanisms. We believe this approach represents a significant advancement in XAI, moving beyond superficial explanations towards truly interpretable and reliable AI systems.

title: Large Language Models as Systems Architects: A Controlled Study of Consensus, Fabrication, and Constraint Reasoning on One Hard Design Task (dataset and analysis code)
abstract: A dataset and analysis comparing how multiple frontier large language models respond to one identical, evidence-demanding systems-architecture prompt: designing a 24/7 autonomous AI development-and-research workstation for a 32 GB Apple M6 Mac mini. Each response is captured verbatim, extracted into a structured decision matrix, and audited for fabricated tools, stale recommendations, hardware-constraint violations, internal contradictions, and citation quality.

title: cpath-triage: diagnostic analysis of verbalized confidence in a medical vision-language model
abstract: Evaluation and analysis code, plus the prediction artifacts behind every table and figure, for a diagnostic study of verbalized confidence in MedGemma-27b-it on colorectal H&E histopathology patches. Covers zero-shot classification, temperature scaling and calibration metrics, selective-prediction routing with explicit tie handling, a design-effect sensitivity analysis in place of clustered intervals, and K=5 prompt-variant consistency routing.Version 4.0 adds a cohort-weighted re-analysis of the K=5 subsets, a wording-only prompt family, image-removal, image-swap and pixel-shuffle controls, and a PLIP image-text baseline.

title: ##基于生物磁场控制的量子比特操控
abstract: This paper investigates the feasibility and potential of utilizing biological magnetic fields for quantum bit (qubit) control and manipulation. The core concept involves leveraging the subtle forces exerted by biological magnetic fields on quantum systems to achieve precise control and entanglement. We propose a system design incorporating a specialized device to generate and control these fields, allowing for targeted interactions with qubits. The theoretical framework presented details the mechanisms involved, exploring the challenges and opportunities associated with this novel approach to quantum information processing. This research explores a potentially disruptive method for qubit manipulation, moving beyond traditional electromagnetic control and offering a pathway for utilizing biological systems in the realm of quantum technologies. We analyze the key factors influencing the effectiveness of this technique, including field strength, qubit sensitivity, and environmental noise. The ultimate goal is to demonstrate the possibility of achieving robust and scalable quantum control using biologically generated magnetic fields. ---

title: Quantum Topology Computation: Adaptive Optimization Framework
abstract: Quantum Topology Computation (QTC) is a novel approach to quantum computation that leverages the inherent quantum properties of topological states to perform complex calculations. This paper introduces a new framework, Adaptive Optimization of Quantum Topology Computation (AOC), designed to dynamically adjust quantum parameters during computation, thereby mitigating errors and enhancing precision. We detail the framework's architecture, focusing on the core mechanism of automated parameter tuning based on a self-adaptive optimization strategy. title: Quantum Geometry Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum geometry-based adaptive algorithm designed to precisely calculate and optimize geometric structures. Traditional optimization methods often rely on manual design, limiting efficiency. Our algorithm leverages the unique properties of quantum geometry to dynamically adjust its parameters, enabling accurate solutions across a wide range of geometric problems. This adaptive approach contrasts with conventional algorithms, offering significant improvements in speed and accuracy. The core mechanism centers on the algorithm's ability to map geometric transformations and constraints to quantum states, facilitating a form of "quantum intuition" in the optimization process. This paper details the algorithm's architecture, introduces key mathematical concepts, and presents preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in a series of challenging geometric optimization tasks.
